Guide.title: Overview
content: A gunslinger with a cause, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/cassidy.png)Cassidy aims true with his ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/peacekeeper.png)Peacekeeper. This cowboy likes to get up close and personal with his enemies where he can enact justice with extreme prejudice. At close to medium range, no one is more lethal than Cassidy. He never wants to get caught out in the open because he can’t travel quickly or far, and can easily get out-ranged.

Finding off-angles where he can close the distance and create crossfire with his team is his primary focus. Additionally, he’s great at protecting his team from flankers due to his burst damage and Hindering ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/flashbang.png)Flashbang. If you can’t be bothered to learn all the flashy hero shooter stuff, Cassidy is a straight shooter who only needs solid fundamentals to succeed.

Guide.title: Playing As
content: * Off angle. Don’t fall into the trap of standing in the center of the payload path or objective area. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/cassidy.png)Cassidy is best when positioned around corners, attacking from the side of his team.
* Stay close. His revolver has severe damage falloff. Stay close to your targets to maximize your damage output.

* Cassidy excels at countering flankers. Use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/flashbang.png)Flashbang to stop them in their tracks and keep your backline safe.

Guide.title: Playing Against
content: * Plan to counter ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/flashbang.png)Flashbang. If your hero has a way to block or dodge Flashbang, be sure to save it when getting into close range against a Cassidy.

* Position outside his optimal range. Many heroes like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ashe.png)Ashe, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/freja.png)Freja, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/zenyatta.png)Zenyatta have the upper hand in long-range fights against Cassidy.

* Watch for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deadeye.png)Deadeye. If you don’t see Cassidy for a bit, he’s likely setting up a flank Deadeye. Stay near cover; you can hide behind it or prepare your counterattack.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Anti-flanker
* Burst damage
* Versatile
* Immobile
* Ultimate issues
* Low range

Guide.title: Anti-flanker
content: Cassidy is one of the best DPS for countering flanking enemies. His combination of burst damage and CC from Flashbang makes him extremely dangerous to dive. He’s also great at protecting his supports from enemy DPS like Sombra and Tracer.

Guide.title: Consistent burst damage
content: Unlike other DPS, whose burst damage comes from cooldowns, Cassidy can burst the enemy at any given moment. Two headshots eliminate 275 HP heroes in a single second! Fan the Hammer is also always a threat of burst damage at very close range.

Guide.title: Versatile offense
content: Depending on the enemy team's comp and his own, Cassidy can adapt his positioning and playstyle to best fit the situation. He can be a Tank buster, anti-dive, anti-flier, a backline assassin, or just hold down the main choke point.

Guide.title: Poor mobility
content: The biggest difference between Cassidy and most DPS is his complete lack of mobility. He’s the least mobile DPS in the entire OW roster. He can’t take high ground, chase down targets, or escape attacks. If the whole team is trying to reposition, Cassidy either stays behind or is the last to arrive.

Guide.title: Inconsistent Ult value
content: Many DPS ults feel like “win buttons.” Deadeye, on the other hand, sometimes gets used just to reload his revolver. Although it has the potential for team wipes, its value is far from guaranteed.

Guide.title: Limited Range
content: Compared to the rest of the ranged hitscan heroes, Cassidy has the worst range. He has the upper hand at close range, but needs to spend time and resources getting into position. Poking at long range is much easier and more consistent. Even projectile heroes like Pharah give him a lot of trouble on maps where she can stay far away while flying.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Peacekeeper
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/peacekeeper.png)Peacekeeper
* Positioning
* * The most important aspect of getting value out of Cassidy’s primary fire is learning how to position. Cassidy is a close to medium range hitscan who can quickly eliminate enemies
* Off angles

* * You’ll want to spend most of your time on slight off angles from your team. You can’t just sit in main and snipe the enemy backline. Repositioning to a side angle allows Cassidy to bypass the enemy tank's main point of defense.
* It’s also safer for both Cassidy and his team as it divides enemy attention.
* Allows you to get a bit closer to your DPS and Support targets as well.
* Flanks
* * Generally, you don’t want to go on hard flanks because of his lack of mobility. It would waste way too much time to slowly walk all the way around the enemy team.

* Soft flanking is what he’s best at. Catching an enemy by surprise who is looking straight ahead gives you the highest chance of a successful flank attack. Be sure to plan how you will deal with the enemy’s response, whether it is an ally Support, health packs, or map cover.
* Main, objective area, and choke points

* * Whether you should stand in the main path and objective area is primarily determined by team composition and matchups. For example, if the enemy is running dive, it’s best to stay near your teammates so you don’t get isolated.

Guide.title: Secondary fire: Fan the Hammer
content: **Tips for Fan the Hammer**
* Burst down Tanks
* * Anytime an enemy Tank gets close to you, Fan the Hammer, Roll, Fan the Hammer is your best anti-tank move.
* Deals 600 damage in less than 3 seconds.
* Chips away at barriers
* * If your best option at the moment is to shoot a barrier, use Fan the Hammer to quickly chip down its health.
* Very close range

* * Any time an enemy is just outside melee distance to you, Fan the Hammer should be considered. The larger the target, the more consistent it is. Good against Bastion, for example, not so great when used on Tracer.
* Finishing hit
* * Don’t let your ego get in the way of eliminating the enemy. If they are one-shot, but you’re not confident in landing the final blow, Fan the Hammer can come in clutch.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Combat Roll
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/combat-roll.png)Combat Roll
* Save for reload
* * Most of the time, you’ll be using Combat Roll for the quick reload. Roughly every other clip, you can alternate between Roll reload and standard reload.
* Tank damage
* * The damage reduction of Combat Roll is extremely important to master. A properly timed Roll will enable Cassidy to survive a Pulse Bomb stick.
* Reduced damage starts immediately upon activating, so use Roll the moment you need extra tankiness.
* Cross up
* * In close-range duels, you can Combat Roll through the enemy to quickly get behind them. Useful in some match-ups, or just to force the enemy to turn around and adjust their aim.

Guide.title: [E] Flashbang
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/flashbang.png)Flashbang
* Anti-dive

* * When the enemy team is diving you or your Supports, Flashbang becomes your most important utility. Hindered prevents the use of movement abilities, so it is one of the best anti-dive abilities in the game.
* Wait until the enemy is low HP or is about to retreat before using Flashbang. Disabling Reaper from using Wraith is game over for him.
* Surprise attack
* * The easiest way to guarantee an elim from a flank is to start with Flashbang, then land your follow-up shots while they are slowed.

Guide.title: Ultimate: Deadeye
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deadeye.png)Deadeye
* Be unpredictable
* * The damage ramps up quickly, so if the enemy is out in the open and not looking away from you, you’ll be far more likely to get elims with Deadeye.
* Get protected

* * If the enemy has high amounts of burst damage or someone who can stun you out of Deadeye, coordinate with your team for the appropriate protection. D.Va’s Defense Matrix in front of you, for example.
* Cancel for Reload
* * A niche tip is that you can activate and instantly cancel Deadeye when you need to quick-reload.
* A common use to melt a Tank is: Fan the Hammer, Roll, Fan the Hammer, Deadeye reload cancel, Fan the Hammer.

Guide.title: Bang Bang
content: * New breakpoints
* * Landing both Flashbangs creates new instakill combos for Cassidy
* * Bang Bang + headshot = 230 Dmg (225HP hero one-shot)
* Best for anti-dive
* * Extra damage and range make Bang Bang the superior choice against enemy DPS and Support flankers.

Guide.title: Even the Odds
content: * Tank damage over time
* * In standard 5v5 games, Cassidy can generate up to 150 HP of self-healing every second. Even if there are only a couple of targets, the extra healing helps to survive against non-burst damage
* If the enemy is running Moira / Juno, for example, neither of them can burst or stun Cassidy, and he’s very likely to survive channeling Deadeye with the extra healing.
* When to avoid picking
* * If the enemy has easy ways of stopping Deadeye with stuns like Sleep Dart, or burst damage like Widow Maker, then the healing is not helpful.

Guide.title: Rollin' Round-Ups
content: * Swap out the close-range burst for more min-range lethality.
* * Silver Bullet crit + plus primary fire body shot will kill 275 HP heroes
* The burst damage is quite good, but you have to sacrifice Fan the Hammer and the sustain Rollin' Round-Up would give you.
* Two Silver Bullet body shots will eliminate 275 HP heroes if the shots are spaced out.
* * Bleed does not stack. You'll need to wait between Silver Bullet shots if you want to maximize damage over time.

Guide.title: Silver Bullet
content: * Swap out the close-range burst for more min-range lethality.
* * Silver Bullet crit + plus primary fire body shot will kill 275 HP heroes
* The burst damage is quite good, but you have to sacrifice Fan the Hammer and the sustain Rollin' Round-Up would give you.
* Two Silver Bullet body shots will eliminate 275 HP heroes if the shots are spaced out.
* * Bleed does not stack. You'll need to wait between Silver Bullet shots if you want to maximize damage over time.

Guide.title: Best Maps
content: Cassidy performs best on maps that encourage medium to close-range fights. Depending on the situation, Cassidy will either be positioned with his team, on an off-angle, or a full-on flank. He doesn’t do much damage at long range, so he struggles on Maps with long sight lines that favor Snipers. Because he has essentially zero mobility, he tends to fall behind on maps with a lot of high ground and on spread-out maps with a lot of ground to traverse.

Guide.title: Watchpoint
content: Gibraltar

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: Team comps built around Cassidy push into the enemy team in stages. Because he lacks mobility and has harsh damage falloff, Cassidy pairs best with teams who keep the fights in close to medium ranges. Tanks that repeatedly contest space by soft engaging, then reengaging, enable Cassidy to position up front with them and keep more enemies in his ideal primary fire range. All he really needs from Supports is reliable healing because he tends to take more damage than the average DPS hero. His damage output is extremely high, so he looks for utility and sustain from his allies.

* **DPS**: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/cassidy.png)Cassidy, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/freja.png)Freja

* **Supports**: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/lifeweaver.png)Lifeweaver, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/kiriko.png)Kiriko

Guide.title: Individual Hero Synergies
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mauga.png)Mauga

* Mauga perfectly fits the bill as a Tank who engages in stages. Although both heroes have long-range capabilities, they are far more effective at closer ranges. Cassidy can adapt to what heroes are trying to counter Mauga as well. If the enemy has an Ana constantly anti-ing Mauga, Cass can go on soft flanks to pressure the Ana and try to force her to use Nade to heal herself.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/freja.png)Freja

* Cassidy's most exploitable weaknesses are his poor range and poor mobility. Freja helps by applying pressure to areas with longer sightlines to contest enemy snipers. She also has the mobility to chase down targets who can evade Cassidy. Both heroes can also follow up on the other's ults because of the threat each poses. Freja utilizes the space Deadeye creates, and Cassidy gets easy follow-up damage off the pull-in effect of Bola Shot.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/lifeweaver.png)Lifeweaver

* As stated in the above section on team comps built around Cassidy, he primarily needs high amounts of consistent healing from his Supports. Lifeweaver has no trouble keeping Cassidy alive in the face of danger. He can also use Pedal Platform to raise up Cassidy to strong high ground positions or get a sneaky vertical angle during Deadeye. Additionally, Cassidy can go for deeper flanks than usual for a backline assassination of flank Deadeye because he knows Lifeweaver can pull him out at any moment.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: Cassidy is a monster is the close to mid-range, but his damage quickly falls off the farther away he is. Position outside his optimal range. Many heroes like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ashe.png)Ashe, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/freja.png)Freja, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/zenyatta.png)Zenyatta have the upper hand in long-range fights against Cassidy.

The main thing you need to deal with is ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/flashbang.png)Flashbang. If you plan on approaching him, you need to counter ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/flashbang.png)Flashbang by either dodging it with a mobility or invulnerable ability like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/dancing-blaze.png)Dancing Blaze, or block with something like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deflect.png)Deflect or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/barrier-shield.png)Barrier Shield

Watch for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deadeye.png)Deadeye. If you don’t see Cassidy for a bit, he’s likely setting up a flank Deadeye. Stay near cover; you can hide behind it or prepare your counterattack. Don't forget you can stun him to cancel the ult with attacks like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/javelin-spin.png)Javelin Spin and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sleep-dart.png)Sleep Dart.

Guide.title: Overview
content: Using her tech to harness the power of hard-light, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/symmetra.png)Symmetra creates Photon beams, orbs, Barriers, and Teleporters. Although she has some notable weaknesses, her unique abilities to instantly reposition herself and her entire team will forever keep her as a viable hero pick.

Sym generally plays up front with her Tank, where she can get the most use out of her high damage beam. Even at longer ranges, her orbs deal a good amount of damage, so even though they are slow, watching them fly at you applies a lot of pressure. On any map where there is only one direction for the enemy team to approach you, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sentry-turret.png)Sentry Turrets are one of the best abilities to make sure the enemy never makes it through alive.

Guide.title: Playing As
content: * Against Tanks with barriers, focus their shield with your primary fire to ramp up damage and restore your ammo. Once the barrier is down, walk in and melt everyone.
* Place Turrets behind you to watch your Flank. They’ll autofire and thwart those trying to sneak up on you.

* ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/teleporter.png)Teleporter can be used to get your entire team past an enemy stronghold at choke points. Try to get your team to high ground or natural cover behind the enemy.

Guide.title: Playing Against
content: * Shoot the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sentry-turret.png)Sentry Turrets. Don’t be the teammate who walks forward, gets blasted by the turrets, and ignores them. On corners, you can quickly peek and fire before they target you.
* Watch for TP. Her team might end up behind you and wipe your backline. Sym may also use TP to dive an isolated target, so always watch to see if her hands are up in the deploy animation.
* Stay out of her effective range. Primary fire and turrets both have very limited ranges, so most heroes have the advantage against Sym at medium to long range.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Repositioning
* Control
* High DPS
* Low range
* Weak versus poke and dive
* Difficult to coordinate with team

Guide.title: Repositioning
content: As the only hero with a Teleporter, Sym enables her entire team to reposition to places that would be impossible without her. Once deployed, the teleportation is instant and can be used both ways. From casual play to pro OWCS, we see game-winning plays made possible by sneaky Teleporter placement.

Guide.title: Area control
content: Sentry Turrets excel at area control because three can be deployed at a time and they inflict a slow debuff on their target. Whether she’s using Turrets to hold a choke, defend the objective area, or patrol her flank, once Sym has set up, it’s difficult to take that space back from her.

Guide.title: High DPS
content: Between a level 3 beam and 3 turrets, Sym can deal a whopping 270 damage per second! Even her orb deals 100 burst damage. When she’s able to keep holding primary fire, Sym destroys her targets.

Guide.title: Limited range
content: Although Sym’s right-click has infinite range, she's much more effective within range for her beam. She's not very mobile or tanky, so getting into beam range poses a lot of danger to herself. Typically, she'll have to deal with enemy tanks first, and most of them can run her over.

Guide.title: Weak to poke and dive
content: Sym tends to fit best when both comps are running brawl or rush comps. She struggles to keep up with her own team’s mobility if they are running dive heroes. When the enemy runs dive, they have an easier time playing around her turrets and can easily collapse on Sym. Her TP makes her easy to chase for high mobility heroes as she can only go to one of two places. Additionally, poke heroes counter Sym by staying out of her range and outputting more consistent damage.

Guide.title: Difficult to coordinate with the team
content: When playing Sym, you may come up with an awesome TP strategy, but actually getting your team to coordinate positioning and timing with you ends up being quite the challenge. Your Tank may not protect you while setting up TP, some allies get left behind, and more often than not, your team has no idea what to do or where to go after taking the TP.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Photon Projector
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/photon-projector.png)Photon Projector
* Maintain high level

* * At level three, your beam deals triple its base damage. Try to keep the level up by continuously dealing damage. Even deployables build and maintain charge, so if the enemies are out of range, you can shoot turrets, barriers, and other deployables to keep your level up.
* Barrier Tanks
* * Against enemies with barriers, use their shield to manage your ammo. Damaging a barrier with beam consumes no ammo and instead restores your supply.
* Begin by focusing the barrier to ramp up your level, then switch to attacking the hero. You can always switch back to the barrier if your ammo gets low.
* Sym’s gun has a level indicator
* * Most players never notice this, but on Symmetra’s gun, there is a level indicator on the back. Level 1 will display a single red circle, and level three will display three red circles.

Guide.title: Secondary Fire: Photon Projector (charged orb)
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/photon-projector.png)Photon Projector **(charged orb)**
* Poke

* * Although the travel speed is very low, the large projectile is fairly easy to get direct hits with across longer ranges. Whenever you are outside of your primary fire range, you should be spamming fully charged orbs.
* Jiggle peek
* * Because it takes a full second to max charge an orb, you should always be behind barriers or cover when charging. Standing in the open while charging just lets the enemy attack you for free.
* Only peek the moment before firing.
* Duel

* * When you get into 1v1 duels, orbs are really good because you can play the corners, charge up, and peek to fire. By doing so, you’ll be dealing more damage in most matchups thanks to the 100 burst damage of each orb.
* This technique is even more effective when using Shield Battery Major Perk since you’ll also be healing while charging.
* Against snipers, you can corner peek and crouch spam to dodge headshots.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Sentry Turret
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sentry-turret.png)Sentry Turret
* On defense
* * Whenever your team is already holding the objective, you should set up turrets above the main choke point so the enemy has to deal with them whenever they try to approach the objective.
* On maps with more side paths, save a Turret to place behind you and watch your flank. The enemy won’t be able to attack you from that doorway or angle without you knowing.
* On attack

* * When approaching the enemy, you can deploy turrets above and behind the enemy team. That way if they start retreating from you’re primary fire, they’ll walk into your turrets' damage and slow debuff.

* Target the enemy backline. You may need to find an off angle to do so but it's worth the extra time. Supports generally can’t destroy turrets as fast, and any time they take to do so means they aren’t healing their team.
* Turret bomb
* * Any turrets you place on the ground will be teleported if you place the TP on top of them.
* Try placing all your turrets on the ground, then deploying the TP just behind the enemy to instantly attack them with all your turrets.

Guide.title: [E]: Teleporter
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/teleporter.png)Teleporter
* Flanks and dives
* * You can use TP just for yourself to get around the team and go for backline assassinations. Then you can always TP away if their counterattack gets too intense.
* Reposition teammates
* * Particularly useful with low mobility allies, TP to get your team around is the most powerful use of the ability.
* On the occasions where the enemy team is full holding you at the choke point, one TP can get your team past them and switch roles as you guys effectively become the new defenders.
* 1v1s

* * Anytime you get into a 1v1 duel, you should deploy a TP as soon as possible. TP to dodge their attacks, and mix up their aim. Even just standing near the TP is a mental mixup because they’ll be expecting you to TP, but be unsure of when.
* Mix up your timing by TPing quickly back and forth, or staying on one end longer than the other.

Guide.title: Ultimate: Photon Barrier
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/photon-barrier.png)Photon Barrier
* Divide the battlefield
* * 99% of the time, you’ll want to split the objective in half, whether that be front to back or left to right, is up to you to divide in the moment.
* This lets your whole team shield dance the enemy team, and ensures your Barrier is where the fight is happening.
* Can the enemy run away?

* * Before placing your Barrier, ask yourself if the enemy can move out of your LoS. If they can back up, and still contest the objective, or have enough time to wait your ult out, then you’ll have wasted your ult.
* Counter ult
* * Some ultimates, like Tac Visor, can be easily blocked on reaction to hearing the activation voice line. Saving your team from an enemy ult is a great use of Photon Barrier.

Guide.title: Sentry Capacity
content: * Patrol and extra flank angle

* * Sentry Capacity is useful to select when the enemy has been flanking you and giving you trouble. You can place one turret on both sides of you, and still have two more to use as you normally would to attack the enemies in front of you.
* More choke pressure

* * Make a semi-circle around the main choke and watch the enemy team get blasted from every angle. Although they can still destroy them, it takes more time and they’ll have suffered more damage in the process.
**Advanced Teleportation**
* Best Minor Perk
* Why you want the extra TP distance
* * Sym doesn’t have to get so close to her desired TP location, which means her deploy positioning is safer.
* When bypassing choke points, you can get your team farther behind the enemy, which often results in a more advantageous position.
* Better escapes
* * When using TP to disengage, you create even more distance between you and your attackers which gives you a higher chance of surviving.
* Dive deep into the backline
* * When the enemy team has a Sniper sitting way in the back who isn’t dying, TP all the way back to them and take them out.

Guide.title: Perfect Alignment
content: * Max range
* * At level 3 your beam will gain 3.6 extra meters of range for a total of 15.6 meters.
* Counter brawl and rush
* * Against close range and melee enemies, Perfect Alignment will help you outrange them and be able to attack while taking less damage.
* Paired with a speed boost like Lucio or Juno’s Hyper Ring, Perfect Alignment is even stronger because you can get in close to level up your beam, then back up with the extra range.

Guide.title: Hovering Barrier
content: * Max range
* * At level 3 your beam will gain 3.6 extra meters of range for a total of 15.6 meters.
* Counter brawl and rush
* * Against close range and melee enemies, Perfect Alignment will help you outrange them and be able to attack while taking less damage.
* Paired with a speed boost like Lucio or Juno’s Hyper Ring, Perfect Alignment is even stronger because you can get in close to level up your beam, then back up with the extra range.

Guide.title: Shield Battery
content: * Best for duels and flanks
* * If you find yourself spending more time flanking and 1v1ing the enemy than you do on the frontline, then Shield Battery is the better Major Perk for you.
* Receiving constant self-healing comes in clutch to win more duels and flank more aggressively.
* The tether visually indicates you’re in range and receiving healing.
* Refer to _“Tips for Teleporter”_ for a breakdown of offensive strategies to employ with TP.

Guide.title: Maps
content: The best maps to play ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/symmetra.png)Symmetra on either have enclosed objective areas or funnel both teams into one main choke point. On maps with either of these qualities, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sentry-turret.png)Sentry Turret put in crazy work. The enemy has no other pathing or position options but to walk in and deal with your turrets.

Because of her limited primary fire range, Sym also does better on maps with shorter sight lines and worse on maps with long sight lines. The more open an area is, the more space the enemy team has to play outside of her range and away from her turrets.

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/symmetra.png)Symmetra has two playstyles. One is to use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/teleporter.png)Teleporter to flank and turret bomb the backline. The other is to play with the Tank, build charge, then melt everyone. To maximize the safety and consistency of the dive style, she needs at least one other hero who can dive with her (on their own or by using the TP).

To play as a frontliner, she wants her Tank to hold the front so she can safely push up with them (e.g. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/reinhardt.png)Reinhardt, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ramattra.png)Ramattra, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/junker-queen.png)Junker Queen). Because she has limited range on her primary fire, she can't stand back and poke, but she also can't push up on her own.

The best aggressive pairings for Supports are ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/lucio.png)Lúcio for speed or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/brigitte.png)Brigitte for synergy of similar brawl-hybrid playstyles. Symmetra gives Brigitte much-needed mobility through her TP. The range of Repair Packs and TP is nearly identical as well, which enables Symmetra and her allies to be on opposite ends of the TP from Brigitte and still receive her healing. Anyone who gets TP dived by Brigitte and Symmetra is instantly dead because of their high damage and sustain combo.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/symmetra.png)Symmetra's team has ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/teleporter.png)Teleporter, so expect them to get to point first on Control Maps unless you have speed boost and very mobile heroes. When she's already set up, you need to destroy ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sentry-turret.png)Sentry Turrets ASAP. Don't let your team walk and get blasted by turrets and don't expect your teammates to be smart enough to find them.
Shoot the turrets. Don’t be the teammate who walks forward, gets blasted by the turrets, and ignores them. On corners, you can quickly peek and fire before they target you.
Watch for TP. Her team might end up behind you and wipe your backline. Sym may also use TP to dive an isolated target, so always watch to see if her hands are up in the deploy animation.
Stay out of her effective range. Primary fire and turrets both have very limited ranges, so most heroes have the advantage against Sym at medium to long range.

Guide.title: Overview
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/soldier-76.png)Soldier: 76 is the premier, beginner-friendly, all-rounder of Overwatch. Based on a first-person shooter kit, his abilities are easy for newcomers to understand.

The unique ability to sprint facilitates an off-angle playstyle where he’s constantly repositioning. Armed with an assault rifle with zero bullet spread means Soldier: 76 can be a deadly marksman at all distances. Finish off his kit with an aimbot ultimate, and he’s easily one of the most reliable heroes to play.

Guide.title: Playing As
content: * Use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sprint.png)Sprint to run around the sides of maps and attack the enemy from a different angle than the rest of your team.

* ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/helix-rockets.png)Helix Rockets is your best burst of damage. Try not to shoot them into barriers and other damage-mitigating abilities.

* Combo ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/tactical-visor.png)Tactical Visor with a boost such as ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/nano-boost.png)Nano Boost, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/orbital-ray.png)Orbital Ray, or Mercy’s ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/caduceus-staff.png)Caduceus Staff to make your Ult more lethal.

Guide.title: Playing Against
content: * Dive him. Every role has heroes who can go with another ally and dive Soldier. He doesn’t have any CC and can’t attack while using his mobility tool.
* Block his poke damage. If all Soldier is doing is shooting barriers, he’s not bringing a lot of value to his team. Either use your own shield or play in the protection of a teammate.
* If you don’t see Soldier in front of you for a while, assume he is about to attack you from your flank. Play near cover so you can escape his surprise attack.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Consistent damage output
* Self sufficient
* Horizontal mobility
* Very long defensive cooldown
* Master of none
* Weak against dive

Guide.title: Consistent damage output
content: Due to his versatile kit, Soldier: 76 is always contributing to a fight. Unlike many other heroes whose value comes in short and infrequent bursts, he never has trouble finding someone to shoot or heal. Whether burning down a barrier, poking with primary fire, or trying to burst an enemy down with Helix Rocket, Soldier’s attacks never cease.

Guide.title: Self sufficient
content: Biotic Field enables Soldier to go on his own solo quests without needing to rely on his team’s resources. A standard gameplay loop looks like run to an off-angle or high ground, Helix and shoot, Biotic Field, shoot, run for health pack, and reposition. All this can be accomplished without ever demanding healing or damage mitigation.

Guide.title: Horizontal mobility
content: As the only hero in Overwatch with infinite ground mobility resource, Soldier’s horizontal mobility is unmatched. He can be very difficult to eliminate because Sprint makes him so evasive. Most enemies have a single charge of their mobility abilities, so Soldier can easily run away.

Guide.title: Very long defensive cooldown
content: At 15 seconds, very few Overwatch abilities have a longer cooldown than Biotic Field. Compared to other long cooldowns like Immortality Field and Life Grip, Biotic Field’s defensive capabilities pale in comparison.

Guide.title: Master of none
content: Although he has a well-rounded kit, Soldier: 76 isn’t the best hero at any particular function. The snipers out-range him, Sojourn has better burst damage and vertical mobility, Bastion is better at burning down barriers, Tracer is more self-sufficient, and the list goes on.

Guide.title: Weak against dive
content: Without any CC or massive burst damage, Soldier is always a dive target. Even though he can Sprint and heal himself, if he gets caught can’t escape, and the healing of Biotic Field is way too low to sustain through a direct attack.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Heavy Pulse Rifle
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/heavy-pulse-rifle.png)Heavy Pulse Rifle
* Zero bullet spread
* * Heavy Pulse Rifle is great for poking and pressuring at long distances because it has zero bullet spread. The only thing you need to worry about is the straight vertical recoil.
* Target prioritization

* * Since Soldier is almost always shooting, selecting who to target is extremely important. Your primary targets should be the backline since you have the range to pressure them. Taking down just half the health of a Support often causes them to retreat, and the other Support to help them. Their tank is then left without either Support’s resources, and you can switch your focus to bursting the Tank down.
* Aim for necks

* * Many players find it helpful to aim for the necks of their targets so they get in a mixture of headshots and bodyshots. The high rate of fire makes landing hits consistent, so going for headshots when possible is worth it.

Guide.title: Secondary Fire: Helix Rocket
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/helix-rockets.png)Helix Rockets
* Helix first

* * When you catch an enemy who doesn’t see you, always Helix Rocket first since it is a travel projectile. Depending on the distance, waiting until just before the Helix lands, then shooting primary fire will deliver your biggest burst of damage and is often enough to instantly get the elim!
* AoE damage

* * The steady damage of Pulse Rifle often gives enemies time to fall back to cover. Using the splash damage of Helix Rocket to explode on the ground next to them can secure the kill on a target who was escaping with low HP.
* Rocket jump

* * Shoot Helix at your feet and jump to get extra height and distance in your jump. This can be useful for jumping from one high ground area to another, or getting onto a ledge just a bit too high for your normal jump to reach.

Guide.title: [E]: Biotic Field
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/biotic-field.png)Biotic Field
* Don’t waste it if your life isn’t in danger

* * The long 15-second cooldown means Soldier players need to be picky about when to use and when to save Biotic Field. Don’t just throw it down when no one is attacking or just because you assume some will.
* Play more passively after trading

* * If the enemy trades their cooldowns with yours, you’ll need to play more passively until Biotic Field is back up. For example, Enemy Winston Jump Packs you, so you have to run away and Biotic Field to live. Winston will have his leap back, and you’ll still have about 10 seconds before you can use Biotic Field again, so position yourself safely where your team can help you.
* Heal your team

* * Giving your entire team up to 200HP each can turn a close fight, into a won fight. Typically, you’ll use Biotic Field just for yourself, if you see your team needs the healing, don’t hesitate to put it down and keep your allies alive.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Sprint
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sprint.png)Sprint
* Constantly reposition

* * Soldier is strongest when he’s unpredictable. If you stand in the same spot or always fire around the same corner, his damage is easy to survive. Use Sprint and keep changing where you are attacking from. Change up which side, high ground, and flanks are all strong options for him.
* Strafe Sprint
* * When running away from an enemy, don’t just run in a straight line because you’ll be easy to hit. Strafe from side to side while running away, and you’ll be slipping and dodging those attacks.

Guide.title: Ultimate: Tactical Visor
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/tactical-visor.png)Tactical Visor
* Know the enemy team's options

* * Does the enemy have a Reinhardt shield to protect them? Is there structures and covers they can quickly hide behind? Are there multiple enemies with the mobility to jump on you? You need to ask yourself these questions before deciding to use Tac Visor.
* If they have a shield tank for example, either wait until the barrier is destroyed or run around the enemy to an angle where targets can’t be protected by the tank.
* Best when damage boosted.

* * Nano Visor is one of the most classic and strong Ult combos in Overwatch. Additionally, you could get boosted by Mercy, Orbital Ray, Kitsune Rush, or go for Discord Targets. Depending on your team comp, be sure to plan how to amplify your damage during Visor and you’ll have significantly more success with the ult.

Guide.title: Helix Propulsion
content: * The best Minor Perk, you can effectively increase each ammo clip by 50% if you time one Helix Rocket per clip.
* Ammo doesn’t overfill
* * Make sure to wait until you have 15 bullets or fewer to use your Helix in order to maximize reload efficiency.
**Field Emergency**
* Situational at best
* * Very few times per match will you find yourself measurably benefiting from being able to heal low HP allies quicker.
* Soldier doesn't want to wait around near his allies for them to be at critical health. He’s typically not positioning right next to his allies and wants to use Biotic Field on himself.
* Extra ult charge
* * You can build Ult faster through healing stats if you keep using Biotic Field Perk to farm healing off your allies.

content: * The best Minor Perk, you can effectively increase each ammo clip by 50% if you time one Helix Rocket per clip.
* Ammo doesn’t overfill
* * Make sure to wait until you have 15 bullets or fewer to use your Helix in order to maximize reload efficiency.
**Field Emergency**

* * Very few times per match will you find yourself measurably benefiting from being able to heal low HP allies quicker.

* Extra ult charge
* * You can build Ult faster through healing stats if you keep using Biotic Field Perk to farm healing off your allies.

Guide.title: Agility Training
content: * When matched up against multiple dive enemies, Agility Training can be the better Major Perk to select. Escaping faster and not having to stop to reload increases uptime without sacrificing evasive maneuvers.
* If Biotic Field is deployed, Sprint around inside it while reloading to keep dodging and healing until reloading has finished.

Guide.title: Stim Pack
content: * Heal or boost

* * Since you don’t lose the option to use Biotic Field for healing if needed, Stim Pack allows for some versatility. Turn Soldier into a glass cannon as he gains attack speed at the cost of being anti-healed.
* The short 4-second window means you’ll want to know and see your target before activating Stim Pack, or else you risk wasting the long CD.
* Cleanse effects

* * Abilities like Protection Suzu, Projected Barrier, and Life Grip will cleanse the anti-heal effect. This is especially good when using Stim Pack for Tac Visor, as the enemy team will likely all turn and focus you.

Guide.title: Maps
content: The best maps to play Soldier: 76 on are maps with lots of flank routes. Having excellent ground mobility, but not vertical mobility, means flat levels maximize his Sprint value and minimize his vertical weakness. If the high ground areas are easily accessible, however, he should certainly be looking to take them. You’ll also want to look for longer sight lines as his weapons are best suited for medium-range engagements. Maps that force close-quarters combat are difficult for Soldier as he gets outclassed by heroes like Tracer and Genji. Really long sight lines are also a problem for him if the enemy is running snipers like Widow Maker.

Guide.title: Watchpoint
content: Gibraltar

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/soldier-76.png)Soldier: 76 is one of the most self-sufficient heroes in all of Overwatch thanks to his mobility and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/biotic-field.png)Biotic Field. He doesn't directly need any particular heroes on his team to run around the map and do some soft flanking.

Barrier Tanks are nice to have since they offer great protection for him to spam the main lines. However, Rush and Dive Tanks get good value as well since he can keep up with their pace and follow up with damage from range for focus fire and quick kills.

The best Supports for him are those with a way to boost his damage output. Most Supports have a way to do this, such as using ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/nano-boost.png)Nano Boost, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/kitsune-rush.png)Kitsune Rush, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mercy.png)Mercy’s damage boost, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/amplification-matrix.png)Amplification Matrix, or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/orb-of-discord.png)Orb of Discord. The other great combo is to fly him around with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/jetpack-cat.png)Jetpack Cat during Tactical Visor.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: The way ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/soldier-76.png)Soldier: 76 carries games is by being uncontested on high ground and flank angles. Therefore, the way to shut him down is to pressure him as soon as he takes an angle on your team.

Dive heroes are the best for the job. His method of dealing with a dive is simply surviving by running away and healing; it's generally not very dangerous to dive him. Every role has heroes who can go with another ally and dive Soldier, even Supports like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/lucio.png)Lúcio and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/jetpack-cat.png)Jetpack Cat.

Track his location, and if you don’t see Soldier in front of you for a while, assume he is about to attack you from your flank. If you lack mobility, play near cover so you can escape his surprise attack. For Tanks, simply blocking his poke damage brings a lot of value. If all Soldier is doing is shooting barriers, he’s not bringing a lot of value to his team. Either use your own shield or play in the protection of a teammate.

Guide.title: Overview
content: Younger brother to Hanzo and close friend of Kiriko, Genji utilizes his cyber-ninja skills to jump, climb, and dash around the fight! One of the two original flanking DPS heroes, Genji remains a great choice for those who want to play behind enemy lines. Wielding his ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/dragonblade.png)Dragonblade and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/shuriken.png)Shuriken give him some of the highest burst damage in Overwatch.

The combination of wall climbing, double jumping, and dashing makes for unmatched agility and mobility. Regardless of map or team comp, Genji always plays best as a flanker or dive hero. When receiving help from teammates, such as coordinating a backline attack with his Tank or getting resources from a Support, he assassinates the enemy backline like no other.
Although Shurikens can be used from any distance, Genji primarily wants to take fights up close and personal after catching enemies by surprise.

Guide.title: Play As
content: * Target Supports. Genji’s primary function is assassinating backlines. Use your mobility to bypass the enemy frontline, get close to the Supports, and kill them first.
* Always flank. Genji shouldn’t ever be standing in the front or middle of objective areas. Position on the perimeter of the fight, and attack from the side or behind the enemy.

* Support players know to save ults like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sound-barrier.png)Sound Barrier to counter Blade. If you suspect they have a defensive ult available, hold on to Blade until your team has forced out their ult.

Guide.title: Play As
content: * Don’t get isolated. Genji is one of the best 1v1 duelists in OW, so stay close to your allies so he always has to fight at least two enemies.

* Force out ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deflect.png)Deflect by dealing damage with your standard weapon, then use your cooldown abilities to punish him when he doesn’t have it.

* ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/dragonblade.png)Dragonblade is extremely lethal and can instantly win team fights. Plan how you will personally survive it, and how you can help your teammates survive with your healing, burst damage, or CC.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * 1v1s
* Mobility
* Killer
* Low poke
* Relies on cooldowns
* Vulnerable to beams

Guide.title: 1v1 duels
content: As one of the best duelers in the game, Genji wants to take on isolated targets as often as possible. Shurikens are easiest to hit from close range because of their slow travel speed. Double jumping over and around his target makes aim tracking a Genji very difficult. The threat of Deflect makes it very difficult for enemy players to use their abilities. Getting their ability Deflected means certain death for the enemy.

Guide.title: Mobility
content: Combining his three mobility tools enables Genji to take paths around the map that are only available to very few other heroes. Genji’s mobility can be used defensively to evade damage, escape fights, or offensively to quickly approach enemies.

Guide.title: Team Kill Potential
content: Dragonblade on its own is a decent ult. When combined with a Support ult like Nano Boost or Kitsune Rush, Genji can realistically wipe out the entire enemy team.

Guide.title: Low poke damage
content: During the Poke phase of a fight, when both teams are still a good distance from each other, Genji provides little value. Spread out Shurikens with slow travel speed are one of the weakest long-range abilities.

Guide.title: Heavily reliant on his cooldown cycle
content: When Genji has already used Deflect and Swift Strike, he becomes a sitting duck defensively, and barely a threat offensively. Players who are able to chain Swift Strike Resets together are incomparably stronger than players who have yet to master the skill.

Guide.title: Vulnerable to beams
content: Because Deflect is Genji’s primary means of surviving, he struggles against heroes with beams. Winston jumps on him, he'd better have dash to get away. If he lets them get into range, heroes like Zarya, Sym, and Moira quickly eliminate Genji.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Shuriken
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/shuriken.png)Shuriken
* Poke
* * Shurikens have no damage falloff. If you see a stationary target like a scoped Ana, a triple headshot deals a quick 162 damage. putting them at critical health.
* Small targets
* * Against small targets, primary fire may feel more difficult to land but the damage potential is much higher than the fan.

Guide.title: Secondary Fire: Shuriken (Fan spread)
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/shuriken.png)Shuriken **(Fan spread)**
* Large body enemies
* * Secondary fire deals consistent high damage into larger body Tanks and DPS. At close range, switch to secondary fire.
* Easier final blows
* * When your target is literally one-shot, secondary fire is typically easier to hit a single Shuriken than primary fire.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Swift Strike
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/swift-strike.png)Swift Strike
* Path to engage
* * In general, do not engage with dash. Instead, use your regular mobility to stage and set up your flanks.
* When to dash
* * Focus on saving Swift Strike to confirm eliminations and get the dash reset, or to disengage and escape with your life.
* Dash Resets
* * Swift Strike’s cooldown resets on eliminations using any ability. You do not have to get the elimination with dash to get the reset.
* Learning how to manage your dash resets is Genji’s most deadly tool, so invest the time needed to learn distance and timing.
* One-shot combo against 250 HP heroes.
* * Primary fire → Swift Strike → Secondary Fire → Melee
* Need to land all Shurikens

Guide.title: [E]: Deflect
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deflect.png)Deflect
* Counter the enemy's highest value ability
* * Save Deflect when you know the enemy team has high-value abilities such as: Sleep Dart, Cardiac Overdrive, Sticky Bombs, Graviton Surge, Bastion turret form, etc.
* Cooldown cycle
* * Do not engage in close-quarters combat without Deflect available. Once you’ve used it, you need to plan how you will survive or escape.
* Just saving Deflect creates the threat of its use, which is almost as valuable as having an additional cooldown ability when dueling opponents.
* When the enemy knows you still have Deflect, they’ll be hesitant to use their abilities.
* Aiming Deflect
* Deflect’s hitbox is only in front of Genji and does not stop damage from behind. Therefore, you need to be aiming at your attacker to Deflect their attack.
* Example: Deflect a scoped shot from Widowmaker back at her head, and you’ll kill her with a critical hit.

Guide.title: [SPACE]: Cyber-agility
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/cyber-agility.png)Cyber-Agility
* Staging and pathing
* * Whenever possible, find ways to engage backline targets by only using wall climb and double jump. This allows Genji to always have Swift Strike available for actual combat.
* Get creative and find ways to surprise the enemies by attacking from unexpected angles. This will also minimize the damage you take during the setup phase.

Guide.title: Ultimate: Dragonblade
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/dragonblade.png)Dragonblade
* Track enemy counter abilities

* * Before using Dragonblade, it is extremely important to see enemies use the cooldowns that could shut you down (Ana Sleep Dart, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/transcendence.png)Transcendence, Cassidy Grenade, etc).
* Likewise, heroes who have high mobility or invincible escapes shouldn’t be targeted unless you’ve seen those abilities used.
* Look for isolated targets
* * Anytime you can find an enemy position far from the rest of their team, they’ll be the easiest to kill and get the first dash reset from.
* Coordinate with ally abilities
* * The classic combo for using NanoBlade is to call for Nano Boost by dashing up into the air, popping both ults, then using the dash reset to dive your target.
* Depending on your team composition, determine the abilities that will empower your Dragonblade to have the highest chance of getting kills.
* Dragonblade bread and butter combos
* * Eliminates 275 HP heroes: Dash → slash → slash (dash cooldown reset), repeat.
* (With Nano): Dash → slash eliminates 225 HP heroes.

Guide.title: Swift Cuts
content: * Best Minor Perk
* * Lifesteal during Dragonblade enables you to be even more aggressive than normal during your ult.
* Less reliant on team resources
* * When running Dragon’s Thirst, Genji has more agency to make big plays without the need for healing or comboing with ults like Nano Boost.
* When swinging repeatedly, Genji gains up to ~45 healing per second, and with Nano, it jumps up to ~70 healing per second!
* Still not invincible
* * Always remember that just because you are lifestealing, you aren’t invincible, so take your standard precautions and don’t try to 1v5 the enemy team.

Guide.title: Dragon's Thirst
content: * Best Minor Perk
* * Lifesteal during Dragonblade enables you to be even more aggressive than normal during your ult.
* Less reliant on team resources
* * When running Dragon’s Thirst, Genji has more agency to make big plays without the need for healing or comboing with ults like Nano Boost.
* When swinging repeatedly, Genji gains up to ~45 healing per second, and with Nano, it jumps up to ~70 healing per second!
* Still not invincible
* * Always remember that just because you are lifestealing, you aren’t invincible, so take your standard precautions and don’t try to 1v5 the enemy team.

Guide.title: Blade Twisting
content: * More damage, ult charge, and elims

* * More damage is more good. But, you'll need to use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/swift-strike.png)Swift Strike late in your combos to ensure you get the bonus damage.

* Against the 175 HP heroes ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/tracer.png)Tracer and pilot ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/d-va.png)D.Va, the extra 25 damage makes ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/swift-strike.png)Swift Strike > ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/dragonblade.png)Dragonblade slash kill.

Guide.title: Meditation
content: * Significantly increase survivability
* * Restore up to 70 health during Deflect. The extra health enables Genji to stay in fights longer, and thereby deal more damage.
* Help with beams
* * While 35 healing per second is lower than the damage per second of every beam, it will still help Genji to survive some situations where he would’ve otherwise died.

Guide.title: Numbani
content: * * The first two points on Numbani have tons of high ground surrounding the point and path of the payload. Superior vertical mobility allows Genji to take advantage of the various high ground areas for both defensive and offensive positions. On the final point, there are multiple strong flank routes Genji can use to set up engagements on vulnerable backlines.

Guide.title: Dorado
content: * * Dorado is full of walls in every area of the map that Genji can climb up to take advantageous positions. The defending team's high ground position on the first point is incredibly strong. Genji is one of the few heroes who can reliably contest this position or climb up and bait out multiple cooldowns with Deflect.

Guide.title: Circuit Royal
content: * * The sightlines on Circuit Royal are super long. Although Genji’s Shurikens have no falloff damage, other DPS heroes with more reliable ranged damage abilities tend to outperform him here. First point Circuit Royal tends to be the most difficult map area of any map for Genji to find value on.

Guide.title: Havana
content: * * First and third point are wide open spaces with nowhere for Genji to hide, retreat, or safely attack from. Long-range heroes like Sojourn and Widow have a fairly easy time picking off Genji while he’s still trying to make his way forward. Second point attacking is a bit easier for him, but defense here also makes it hard for Genji to find value.

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: Team comps built around mobility can best utilize Genji’s power. Full dive team comps can be explosive with Genji, but rely on coordination and timing. A team built around strong mobility abilities can completely control a game and dictate when, where, and with whom fights occur.
**Ideal Team Comp built around Genji:**
* Tank: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/winston.png)Winston

* DPS: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/genji.png)Genji, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sojourn.png)Sojourn
* Supports: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana, Lucio

On the other hand, Genji can also play well as the solo dive or flank hero on his team. In these team comps, he functions as an elimination confirmer, following up on team damage. Teammates who output high levels of consistent damage can greatly enable Genji with dash reset after dash reset on low health enemies.

**Example team comp:** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/zarya.png)Zarya, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/genji.png)Genji, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/junkrat.png)Junkrat, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/baptiste.png)Baptiste

Guide.title: Individual synergies with other heroes
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/winston.png)Winston

* Winston is still the best Tank to pair with the Cyborg Ninja. Jump Pack and Swift Strike pair wonderfully with one another. The pair can match each other's aggression and trade between Barrier Projector and Deflect to survive any retaliation to their dive.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana

* The strongest and most famous pairing is based on using both heroes' ults as one: Nano-Blade. A quick YouTube search will flood your feed with countless Nano-Blade montages. Ana’s ranged hitscan healing is also one of the best ways to assist a Genji deep in enemy territory. Landing a big Anti-Nade also allows Genji to quickly follow up with his speed, then dash out to safety.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/kiriko.png)Kiriko

* Protection Suzu can be used as a “get out of jail free” card when Genji makes a mistake and gets hit with a life-threatening ability. Additionally, Kiriko's target-seeking healing is great for consistently healing Genji as he quickly moves around trying to evade damage. When Nano Boost is not available, Kitsune Rush can be just as deadly of a pairing with Dragonblade, allowing Genji to slash at lightning speed.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: Genji struggles against damage types he can’t Deflect (primarily beam damage). The best way for everyone else to shut down a good Genji is by baiting out Deflect. Genji players often save this ability to counter specific cooldowns, so if you can force the use of Deflect to survive against basic damage, you’ll be at a huge advantage.

If using comms, calling out when Deflect and dash are used can help your team know how aggressively they can target the Genji. Most importantly, tracking when Dragonblade is available can easily make the difference between losing and winning the entire game. Most of Genji’s value in a given match revolves around his use of Dragonblade. Therefore, if you are prepared to counter Blade, the Genji player will probably just swap after being flamed by his entire team.

Guide.title: Specific hero counter
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/winston.png)Winston

* The best Tank to pair with Genji is also the best tank to counter him! First off, Genji can’t ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deflect.png)Deflect his ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/tesla-cannon.png)Tesla Cannon. Secondly, Winston can peel for teammates the enemy Genji is focusing and chase down Genji when he attempts to retreat. Lastly, if the Monke has insane juggle mechanics, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/primal-rage.png)Primal Rage beats Dragonblade.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/echo.png)Echo

* Echo’s mobility is very different from Genji’s, but she has the tools to chase him down. At medium range, these two heroes are similarly matched, but ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/focusing-beam.png)Focusing Beam goes through ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deflect.png)Deflect and melts a low HP Genji.

* Echo tends to provide superior value to her team throughout the match when comparing kits without Ults available. Playing Genji into Echo then gives her access to Dragonblade for her Copy, making Echo a devastating foe.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/brigitte.png)Brigitte

* ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/whip-shot.png)Whip Shot alone interrupts Genji's entire game plan. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/swift-strike.png)Swift Strike gets shut down when used as an attack or mobility option when booped by Brig. She also sends out ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/repair-pack.png)Repair Packs, which makes it extremely difficult for Genji to eliminate targets in her range. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/rally.png)Rally can also counter ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/dragonblade.png)Dragonblade by giving everyone armor, and if she lands her stun on the Genji.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/moira.png)Moira

* Moira is the classic Genji counter since her ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/biotic-grasp.png)Biotic Grasp auto-tracks Genji’s fast movement and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/biotic-orb.png)Biotic Orb damages Genji during Deflect unless he directly Deflects the projectile. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/coalescence.png)Coalescence gives Moira a third method of damaging through ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deflect.png)Deflect.

* Additionally, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/fade.png)Fade’s invincibility and movement are also difficult for Genji to deal with and can interrupt him from chaining together dash resets during Dragonblade. Unlike ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/brigitte.png)Brigitte, however, Moira struggles to keep her allies alive against Genji. Moira is an easier way to survive against and kill Genji, but Brig is technically the better counter.
