Guide.title: Overview
content: A long-time favorite of the Overwatch community, the sniper Support hero Ana is simple to play but difficult to master. Landing abilities is the biggest challenge facing any Ana player. Unlike many other Supports, Ana doesn’t have any free value or non-mechanically demanding utility. Ana is often a dive target for the enemy team since she lacks escape abilities, and her primary defense, Sleep Dart, has a long cooldown and can be difficult to land.

Due to her primary fire being used for both healing and damage, she can seamlessly switch between playing offense and defense. If a player can hit their shots, land Biotic Grenades, and Sleep Darts, Ana carries harder than any other Support. Nano Boost on its own is a great Ult to empower an ally to make a big play, and when combined with another Ult, it becomes your team's win condition.

With all long-range abilities, Ana typically wants to be positioned well behind the rest of her team. She assists her team from a safe distance, near cover, where it's difficult for the enemy to target her.

Guide.title: Playing As
content: * Anti-nades are more impactful than healing nades. Even when you need to heal an ally, try to get an enemy with the splash damage of Biotic Nade.
* Scoping makes Ana an easy target. Only ADS when you need the extra precision to land shots and spend most of your time unscoped.
* Nano allies who are already in position to easily attack the enemy. If the enemy can stay away from your Nano’d ally, the ult gets completely wasted.

Guide.title: Playing Against
content: * Sleep Dart is Ana’s primary means of survival. If you see her shoot it or sleep an ally, that is your signal to go attack her.
* When playing Tank or any dive hero, you’ll need to play around anti-nades. Try to predict her timing and use your mitigation or evade ability to make sure you don’t get anti-healed.

* Don’t overcommit to trying to kill her Tank if she hasn’t used Nano in a while. After you use up your cooldowns trying to get the kill, she’ll Nano the Tank, and their counterattack will be too much for you to survive.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Fight-winning abilities
* Balanced damage and healing
* Long Range support
* Low survivability
* High skill floor and ceiling.
* No mobility

Guide.title: Fight-winning abilities
content: Ana’s greatest strength lies in the potential power of Biotic Nade, Sleep Dart, and Nano Boost. Each of these abilities can single-handedly decide the outcome of a team fight. Sleeping an enemy during their ult can prevent a loss, landing the anti-heal on an aggressive tank stops them in their tracks, and a well-timed Nano can teamwipe. The difficulty of doing these things, however, is extremely high. Knowing when to use these abilities, then properly aiming and landing them, and on the right target are all difficult split-second decisions.

Guide.title: Balanced damage and healing
content: As opposed to most Supports, Ana provides her team with high amounts of damage and healing. Both Biotic Nade and Rifle can be used either defensively or offensively. Depending on what her team needs, she can focus on dealing damage or pumping her allies with healing.

Guide.title: Long Range support
content: Ana is the only true sniper Support. She possesses the sole ability to sit in the back of the map area while still providing max value. This also favors her in dive compositions because even though she lacks any mobility, she doesn’t need to physically follow an ally to enable them as they flank or dive the enemy squishies.

Guide.title: Low survivability
content: Ana has very poor survivability. If she is isolated, she almost always loses 1v1 duels and has no way to deal with multiple threats simultaneously. Even if she sleeps an enemy flanker, she still struggles to kill them on her own upon waking up. Her best move is often to sleep, then run away.

Guide.title: High skill floor and ceiling
content: To get even basic value out of Ana, the player needs to be quite mechanically skilled. Genjis know better than any as they’ll jump around mashing “I need healing!” while accidentally dodging every healing shot from their Ana. Although Sleep Dart shuts down just about every ability in the game, its slow projectile speed and long cooldown make it difficult to use efficiently. Landing Anti-nades also often ends without any follow-up since your team only has 3 seconds of no healing to take advantage of.

Guide.title: No mobility
content: Ana's biggest weakness is her lack of mobility. OW has been steadily moving more and more towards a mobility meta game. There is no way for Ana to access high ground, escape from an enemy attack, or quickly reposition herself to follow up on her own team's aggression.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Biotic Rifle
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/biotic-rifle.png)Biotic Rifle
* Healing or damage?
* * Ana will typically be her team's primary source of healing. Prioritize healing, and only deal damage for short windows where your allies aren’t in immediate danger of dying.
* Both hipfire and ADS shots go through full HP allies to heal or damage anyone behind them.
* When to stay unscoped
* * When facing an enemy team with multiple flankers and no one on your team to peel for you, Ana should position closer up with her team.
* Then, she doesn’t need to ADS and can better react to flank attempts.
* When to ADS

* * Try to only ADS when necessary to land the shot. Ana’s strafe speed is significantly slower while scoped, and this makes her an easy target. You also take in a lot more information from the battlefield when unscoped. If you are close to your team or healing a large body hero like a Tank, it's usually better to remain unscoped.
* Switching between ADS and hip fire resists the rechamber animation between shots and makes Ana’s shots per second slower.
* Projectile size
* * The projectile hitbox sizes are affected by being unscoped, ADS, and whether an ally or enemy is targeted.
* ADS against enemies needs to be the most precise, as it has the smallest hitbox
* Unscoped enemy and ally shots are the same medium-sized projectile
* ADS for healing allies are the easiest shots to hit as the projectile is more than 3x the size of ADS damage shots.
* Damage ignores Armor
* * Ana is surprisingly good against enemies with armor health because the damage over time Biotic Rifle shots completely ignore armor's damage reduction.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Sleep Dart
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sleep-dart.png)Sleep Dart
* Sleeping flankers

* * Enemies attempting to dive or flank Ana typically are prepared for Sleep Dart. Generally, it's better to save Sleep Dart until the enemy has used their counter abilities (Genji Deflect, Winston bubble, etc.).

* Ana’s melee animation is visually similar to Sleep Dart's start-up animation and can be used to bait out enemy abilities who are watching to react with their cooldown (ex, Deflect, D.M. Barrier, Mobility cooldown to evade, etc.)
* Stop enemy approaches
* * Whether it's a Ram in Nemesis Form, A Ball swinging in, or a Sojourn sliding right at you, Sleep Dart is the perfect counter to protect yourself and your team.
* If you suspect the enemy will use their cooldowns or ultimates to take space from your team, save Sleep until they are pushing in.
* Use carefully

* * You may often see Ana randomly blasting off a Sleep Dart into a group of enemies, hoping for a random sleep. These are ineffective and low-value, even when they hit. It is better to save the 14-second cooldown.
* Ping your sleeping enemies
* * Because her abilities have a huge impact within small windows of time, pinging enemies you’ve slept, alerts your team that you need assistance.

Guide.title: [E]: Biotic Grenade
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/biotic-grenade.png)Biotic Grenade
* Anti or heal
* * The most powerful use of Biotic Nade is securing elims through anti-healing.
* Look for the situation where the enemy target can’t retreat if hit by an anti-nade to give your team higher odds of getting the KO.
* Self-sustain
* * Nade is Ana’s only source of self-healing outside of the universal passive. In life-or-death situations, it's always best to use Nade on yourself to live.
* However, if you often have to use Nade for self-healing, it indicates a mistake in your positioning.
* Focus on using cover to minimize damage taken, and give your ally Support time to heal you.
* Splash damage
* * Take advantage of the AoE splash of Nade when aiming against shields, barriers, cover, and damage mitigation abilities.
* Genji Deflect has a small hitbox, for example, and you can still Anti him by throwing the Nade on the ground and hitting him with the splash damage.

Guide.title: Ultimate: Nano Boost
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/nano-boost.png)Nano Boost
* Take inventory of both teams’ resources before you Nano

* * The main thing you want to consider when choosing who and when to Nano is what resources are available to both teams. If you Nano a Genji with no Dash and no ult, he will need to waste precious time running around after being Nano’d.
* If you nano a Hog ult when the enemy has Transcendence available, you’ve lost two ults for one enemy ult.
* Nano targets
* * The best Nano targets are heroes with high amounts of burst damage who are already in an offensive position to engage the enemy.
* Also, anytime you have an ally with an ult to combo Nano with, such as Dragon Blade or Tac Visor, try to sync up the timing so you use them together.

Guide.title: Groggy
content: * Best against dive
* * Ana is always a dive priority target, so anything that helps her counter their attacks is huge for her viability.
* The extra damage and slow debuff is basically a guaranteed kill against any hero without an invincible escape tool.
* Shutdown enemy ults
* * Sleep is already one of the best ability counters to ults in Overwatch, but the added slow can give your team the extra space they need to avoid the enemy ult after they awake.
* Ex: Ram ulting at your team, Ana Sleeps him, and by the time he wakes up, then slow walks, your team can get out of his AoE and end his ult early.

Guide.title: Speed Serum
content: * Best when aggressive Nano targets like Reinhardt who struggle to chase down retreating enemies.
* If you absolutely need to, you can Nano the nearest or easiest target just to give yourself the speed boost if you will die otherwise.

Guide.title: Headhunter
content: * Just to flex
* * Refer to the _“Tips for Biotic Rifle”_ section, and you’ll see ADS shots against enemies have a significantly decreased bullet size. This makes landing headshots with Ana quite difficult.
* Additionally, the multiplier is only 1.5x, so the return isn’t that great.

* Head hurtboxes are mostly hidden when looking at the backs of heroes, and you’ll essentially always be looking at the backs of your teammates. Consequently, critical hits on allies are also impractical.

Guide.title: Biotic Bounce
content: * Win button
* * Although the damage and healing are reduced on the 2nd bounce, the anti and heal buffs are the same.
* Potentially, Ana can hit the enemy frontline with the first bounce, then mid or back enemies with the second bounce. Anti-healing on a majority of the enemy team
* Hitting a nade into a wall next to or behind a target is also a very effective means of hitting tricky angles.

Guide.title: King’s Row
content: * * Ana does extremely well on both defense and offense on every point of King’s Row. The many walls throughout the map provide great natural cover for Ana to play around and stay safe while still assisting her team. On defense, try to take high-ground positions before team fights begin so you have more ways to respond to enemy attacks.

Guide.title: Junkertown
content: * * The combination of long sightlines and buildings makes for a great map to play Ana on. The open areas make it difficult for flankers to close the distance on Ana deep in the backline, so generally, this is a map where she can safely position well behind the rest of her team and focus on damage/healing output.

Guide.title: Blizzard World
content: * * Whether running a more brawly or dive team comp, Ana fits into both on Blizzard World. If you have a brawl tank holding the tight chokes or pressing W, stick nearby and hold the ground with them. If your team is mobility-oriented, take a strong position on the perimeter and provide long-range support.

Guide.title: New Junk City
content: * * High-mobility comps dominate New Junk City because of the map's large size. Ana struggles to keep up and often finds herself arriving after the team fight has already been lost. When your team already has control, she does okay, but even then the available positions don’t pair well with Ana’s kit.

Guide.title: Paraíso
content: * * Attacking on Paraíso with Ana feels like a near-impossible task. The defending high ground positions are extremely strong, and the chokes are tight and dangerous for Ana to walk through. Defense can work out okay for her since she can already position herself on high ground. Even then, she still has difficulty keeping up with the fight during rotations, and if she dies first or second, the point is lost since it will take her so long to get back into position.

Guide.title: Antarctic Peninsula
content: * * The three objectives on Antarctic Peninsula only offer Ana two realistic choices. One would be to take a passive position near the back of her team's side of the objective, where she can only get LoS on about 40% of the battle area. The other is to position aggressively forward with the team, where you can provide full support, but are going to be extremely exposed with no escape options.

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: The combination of high healing output and high impact abilities, but also being easy to eliminate, means Ana needs a team that can keep her alive. She can pair great with any team comp, but needs an ally dedicated to peeling for her when being focused. In dive comps, she’s often paired with a Brig to keep her alive against the dive. For poke and brawl comps, she’ll be best paired with Baptiste or Lucio to keep her alive.

Guide.title: Individual synergies with other heroes
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/reinhardt.png)Reinhardt

* Ana gives Reinhardt the perfect amount of burst healing for him to be able to position and swing aggressively. When Rein has Earth Shatter, landing an anti-nade on the stunned opponents pretty much guarantees the fight win. Nano Boost also gets great value when given to a Reinhardt, making his swings two-tap every sub 300hp hero! When facing a Rein mirror, having an Ana to sleep and anti-heal the enemy Rein makes for an easy “tank diff.”
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/genji.png)Genji

* Nanoblade. The synergy of Ana and Genji lies entirely in the game-winning potential of combining their two ults. Nanoblade is one of the hardest ult combos to counter in all of Overwatch and can single-handedly carry games. Ana’s long-range healing also does well to keep Genji up when he is diving the enemy backline.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/brigitte.png)Brigitte

* As stated above, Brigitte’s job in any team comp with Ana is to keep Ana alive and safe against enemy dives. Brig can shut down enemy attacks against Ana so well that Ana is free to focus on supporting her team with healing, damage, and Biotic Nades that carry her team to victory.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: When playing against Ana, no matter your role, you need to keep track of Sleep Dart and Biotic Nade cooldowns. Each is over 12 seconds and gives your team a large window of opportunity to exploit while she doesn’t have them.

When she doesn’t have either, you can safely aggress on her with almost zero risk of dying. The other thing you want to do as often as possible is play out of her LoS. Her lack of mobility means that she can’t follow allies or enemies that are rotating around the map. If you can get her allies to attack you out of her LoS you’ll be at a massive advantage.

Guide.title: Specific Hero Counters
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sigma.png)Sigma

* Sigma’s shield and Kinetic Grasp absorb every single one of Ana’s abilities. The best move for Sigma against an Ana is usually to push his shield between the Ana and the rest of her team. Doing so forces her to reposition since her poke damage is too low to quickly break the shield. Ana has very few counterplay options against Sigma as he can predict when Sleep and Nade will be used and block their effects.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sombra.png)Sombra
* Sombra is one of the easiest heroes to consistently harass and eliminate Ana with. Stealth → Hack → Virus → shoot, wipes Ana and makes it very difficult to reactively Sleep Sombra.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/kiriko.png)Kiriko

* Protection Suzu instantly cleanses Ana’s best abilities: Sleep and Nade. Suzu even cleanses Ana’s primary fire damage over time and can save a hero just before they lose health. Kiriko also tends to win in 1v1 duels against Ana because she can get in, Suzu, then TP out after getting the kill.

Guide.title: Specific Hero Counters names
content: sigma
sombra
kiriko

Guide.title: Overview
content: A stray cat found in Gibraltar and adopted by Brigitte. She pilots a jetpack and is ready to sacrifice all nine lives to protect their team.

Jetpack Cat flies themselves and allies around the map with their unmatched mobility. Their kit benefits from team coordination, sneaky taxiing, and creative playmaking. Lifeline transportation enables unique positioning strategies that have never before been possible in the history of Overwatch!

With high mobility, AoE aura healing, and limited primary fire damage/healing range, Jetpack Cat wants to hover just above the battle. Stay close, but not too close, and reposition frequently to keep your enemies guessing as you maximize your jetpack’s value.

Guide.title: Play As
content: * Fly outside of their range when faced against melee and close combat enemies such as Vendetta.
* Keep repositioning around vertical cover, walls, and structures to keep yourself out of enemy hitscan’s LoS.
* Target Tanks when going to environmental KOs with your ult. When there are no ledges, wait for an ally to use a high damage Ult like Death Blossom.

Guide.title: Play Against
content: * Hitscan heroes are strong against Jetpack Cat. If they are giving you trouble, consider swapping.

* Jetpack Cat doesn’t generate a lot of sustain for their team. If your team has higher healing (Supports like Kiriko and Moira), you win team fights by slowly chipping away at their health while keeping your team alive.
* Immediately start shooting Jetpack Cat when they capture you or a teammate to stop them from getting an environmental KO.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Mobile
* Can transport allies
* Versatile
* Weak vs hitscans
* Ult is risky to use
* Lacks a defensive ultimate

Guide.title: Very Mobile
content: Extremely mobile. Only hero with permanent flying capabilities, and their boost is very fast, and refreshes quickly. Allows her follow up with teammates everywhere or escape defensively.

Guide.title: Transportation
content: Unique playmaking capabilities by transporting allies around the map. Flying ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deadeye.png)Deadeye, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/b-o-b.png)B.O.B., and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/tactical-visor.png)Tactical Visor are just a few of the popular ways to combo ally abilities with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/lifeline.png)Lifeline.

Guide.title: Versatility
content: Versatile and capable of both defensive and offensive playstyles. Her healing output is good when playing like a Support, but she's also one of the best solo-kill assassins in the game. Even after the nerfs, a Claws Out + Territorial will eliminate ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/tracer.png)Tracer without even firing a single shot.

Guide.title: Weak vs range
content: Weak against hitscans and long-range heroes. Anyone who can shoot Cat out of the air makes it difficult for her to utilize her best ability.

Guide.title: Ult is risky to use
content: Ult puts you at risk of being KO’d by enemies that were not knocked down. Even the enemy you grab can shoot and kill you after the stun ends.

Guide.title: Lacks a defensive ult
content: Whereas most Support heroes have an ultimate they can use to save their team from death, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/catnapper.png)Catnapper can only be used offensively. Theoretically, she could use it to stun a solo aggressing enemy like an ulting ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/genji.png)Genji, but generally, she doesn't have a way to save her team from enemy ults.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Biotic Pawjecticles
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/biotic-pawjectiles.png)Biotic Pawjectiles
* No falloff damage, but the projectile only travels 40m before disappearing.
* Pawjectiles are shotgun spread pellets. Each shot is the shape of a cat’s paw. The claws can crit, but the center paw pad cannot crit.
* * Aim towards enemies' necks and upper chest to maximize pellets hit and critical headshot damage.
* Main source of healing and damage. Prioritize healing, and only focus on damage when your teammates are near full HP.

Guide.title: Secondary Fire: Frenetic Flight
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/frenetic-flight.png)Frenetic Flight
* Use the boost to control space and positioning. Optimal range is keeping enemies within primary fire range (40m), and allies within healing aura when using Purr
* Resource-based. After a momentary cooldown, you can reactivate Flight as long as you have remaining fuel.
* Jetpack Cat is extremely evasive and has some of the best mobility in Overwatch.
* * Boost around frequently. Your base flight speed is slow and makes Jetpack Cat an easy target when floating around in the sky.
* Can shoot during boost.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Lifeline
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/lifeline.png)Lifeline
* Transport and heals allies
* Sling shot Cassidy during Deadeye for a lethal surprise Ult!
* The teammate has to press “Interact” to confirm. (Unlike Lifeweaver’s Life Grip)
* * Give your allies time to confirm. It is difficult to quickly yank them out of a fight if they are already at low HP, but it can be a great rescue tool.
* Can NOT shoot during Lifeline.
* No time limit. You can transport your teammate anywhere on the map if you wish.
* * Your teammate CAN shoot and use their abilities while being transported.

Guide.title: [E]: Purr
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/purr.png)Purr
* Knockback upon activation
* Healing increases towards the end of the duration, making it more important to be near allies in the 2nd half of its duration.
* Can be used during Flight and Lifeline, to keep yourself alive while evading attacks, repositioning, and escaping.

Guide.title: Ultimate: Catnapper
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/catnapper.png)Catnapper
* On maps with ledges nearby the objective, save your Ult to use when an environmental KO is possible.
* Low damage, so not lethal on its own. Try to combo with another teammate’s burst damage Ultimate, like Anran’s Ascent.

* Keep in mind that even if you slam into knockdown multiple enemies, if the opposing team has hitscans like Ana and Emre elsewhere on the map, they can easily KO you as you pick up and carry their teammate.
* * Use Purr and Flight immediately after ulting to stay alive.

* Bonus Tip: Against Tanks like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/d-va.png)D.Va who fly after being dropped, don't detach. Instead, use Descend to dip them below the environmental KO threshold off the ledge, then fly away immediately after.

Guide.title: Passive: Jetpack
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/jetpack.png)Jetpack
* Just because you can perma-fly at the top of the ceiling, doesn’t mean you should.
* Make sure you stay in range of your own abilities.
* Flying too high where there is no environmental cover to hide behind makes you an easy target and will get you killed quickly.

Guide.title: Ulterior Motive
content: * Refills fuel even during ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/frenetic-flight.png)Frenetic Flight.
* Significantly increases mobility and flight uptime when you are healing.
* Dealing Damage does not convert into fuel.
* Recommended default Minor Perk

Guide.title: Transport Shielding
content: * Best for strategic play-making. Allows you to take more damage while transporting an ally for a flank play. Also makes it safer to go for environmental KOs after your Ult.
* Recommended when playing with comms or frequently coordinating transport plays.

Guide.title: Headbutt
content: * Need to have almost half fuel and to travel ~8m to build enough momentum for the boop. (Displayed as VFX circling your screen)
* Works in transport mode
* Pair with Ulterior Motive for more frequent use.

Guide.title: Claws Out
content: * Best for consistent aggressive plays. If your team is using an aggressive closerange strategy such as brawl, rush or dive, having extra damage every 6-seconds on your melee is quite powerful.
* When your team is playing more distance or poke styles, you won’t have many opportunities to use Claws Out.
* Recommended Major Perk

Guide.title: Maps
content: The best maps for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/jetpack-cat.png)Jetpack Cat have plenty of vertical structures for her to fly around. High ground is especially strong since she can perma-fly. Numbani, Watchpoint: Gibraltar, and Paraiso, for example, all feature structural layouts that enable her to constantly reposition safely.

Flatter maps and those with wide open objective areas such as Samoa, Havana, and New Queen Street don't offer nearly as much room to play. On these maps, you'll typically need to position closer to your team and use them for safety.

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: Jetpack Cat is extremely self-sufficient thanks to their combat ability, mobility, and self-sustain. Because of this, she doesn't need allies to sit around and protect her.

Heroes who can fly or move quickly are no problem to keep up with, so look for teammates like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/d-va.png)D.Va, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/echo.png)Echo, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/tracer.png)Tracer and be ready to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/frenetic-flight.png)Frenetic Flight in to assist in their attacks.

For a second Support it depends on the rest of your team more than the specific pairing. If your team has a tank like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mauga.png)Mauga or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/reinhardt.png)Reinhardt who demand a lot of healing resources, it's best to pair with someone like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/baptiste.png)Baptiste.

However, if your team is running full dive or heroes with self-sustain, you can get away with pairing with a lower healing output Support like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/lucio.png)Lúcio or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/brigitte.png)Brigitte.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: To coutner ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/jetpack-cat.png)Jetpack Cat, you need to pressure her every time she exposes herself. Even a bit a damage will force her to back off, which is especially good when she's using ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/purr.png)Purr.

Always be ready for a flank attack because she can fly in super fast and shoot you from the side. Don't tunnel vision, and if you have any CC, you can save it if you've noticed the Cat player keeps going for flanks.

Also, you can counterswap in your role to heroes like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/d-va.png)D.Va, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ashe.png)Ashe or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/illari.png)Illari to have an easier time shooter ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/jetpack-cat.png)Jetpack Cat out of the sky, evading her ult, and shutting down her flanks.

content: dva
ashe

Guide.title: Overview
content: The young member of the Hashimoto, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki, joins the roster as he helps Talon to infiltrate the Yokai in Kanezaka. There is a fear he may be caught between loyalties, but his skills cannot be ignored.

Compared to other supports, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki wants to play and position aggressively. Staying up close to the main team fight allows him to deal more damage, which in turn charges his healing abilities.

When the action starts getting too dangerous for his liking, he can halt his attackers with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/binding-chain.png)Binding Chain, escape with his teleport, and activate self-healing. Mizuki has all the tools a hero needs to take games into their own hands, be a playmaker, and carry games.

Guide.title: Play As
content: * Prioritize offense. Your healing is higher the more you deal damage.

* Save ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/binding-chain.png)Binding Chain to use on enemies that get past your Tank. Keep them trapped and secure the elim.

* Use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/kekkai-sanctuary.png)Kekkai Sanctuary to protect and heal your team, and to counter projectile Ults such as Soujourn’s Overclock.

Guide.title: Play Against
content: * Stay outside his effective range. His abilities are close to medium-ranged, so attack him from distances where he cannot coutner attack.
* His single-target healing is low; you can burst down his allies even when he’s trying to heal them.
* Go inside his ultimate and force his team out. If you have melee or beam abilities, you can penetrate the Sanctuary walls.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Passive healing
* Good CC
* Aggressive Tools
* Ultimate limitations
* Needs to group
* Limited range

Guide.title: Passive healing
content: Passive healing allows ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki to focus on dealing damage and securing eliminations. He should be a strong source of damage for his team in every match.

Guide.title: Good CC
content: Powerful crowd control in ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/binding-chain.png)Binding Chain. It's like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/flashbang.png)Flashbang and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/whip-shot.png)Whip Shot rolled into one ability. Tethering any flanker will allow your team to get the kill unless the enemy team uses high value defense utility such as ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/life-grip.png)Life Grip or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/barrier-projector.png)Barrier Projector.

Guide.title: Aggressive nature
content: Can play and position aggressively and has the tools to duel and keep himself alive. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/katashiro-return.png)Katashiro Return is built specifically to go in, attack, and get out for free.

Guide.title: Ult is only good vs projectiles
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/kekkai-sanctuary.png)Kekkai Sanctuary is only effective against projectile poke comps. Weak against dive and melee heroes. It also offers much less sustain than similar defensive ults.

Guide.title: Need to stick with team
content: Needs to stay positioned near allies to benefit from AoE healing. However, limited movement capabilities make it difficult to keep up with high-mobility allies.
If there's no ally nearby or in his LoS, he can't use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/healing-kasa.png)Healing Kasa to heal himself.

Guide.title: Limited-range
content: Limited range combined with low-mobility means he is constantly in vulnerable to the enemy team making an aggressive play for him. He also has little counterplay against fliers.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Spirit Glaive
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/spirit-glaive.png)Spirit Glaive

* Limited range, but no bounce limit. Attack enemies inside rooms or around corners with ricochets. Positions where you can hit the enemy but they can’t hit you are ideal for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/spirit-glaive.png)Spirit Glaive.
* All hits inflict impact damage and damage over time.
* The impact damage can crit.

Guide.title: Secondary Fire: Healing Kasa
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/healing-kasa.png)Healing Kasa
* **Needs a target selected to use**. Cannot use Healing Kasa to only self-heal.
* Each bounce grants diminishing healing. Target the ally who needs the most amount of healing, and let your hat auto-bounce to nearby allies.

* The bounces require LoS to track additional allies. If there is a wall or structure blocking the path, the hat returns to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki without using all 3 bounces.

* Use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/healing-kasa.png)Healing Kasa frequently. Try to keep multiple allies nearby, but don’t hesitate to use it even if only one ally needs healing. Two charges and a short cooldown make not using it worst that wasting one.

* * Ideally you want an ally in front of you at all times so you don't have to spin around looking for a target when you need to use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/healing-kasa.png)Healing Kasa

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Katashrio Return
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/katashiro-return.png)Katashiro Return

* In n’ Out dives. The primary use for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/katashiro-return.png)Katashiro Return is to initiate an aggressive attack with an ally. Then, TP back to safety before the timer expires.
* 4.5 seconds to TP back, become invulnerable on the return teleport activation.
* Keep in mind the enemy can see the doll, wait for you to TP back to it, and kill you upon return. If you left the doll near enemies, don’t activate the return.
* If you use the speed boost to go aggro, but then get stunned or miss the return TP window, expect to die. Better to use it early and survive than wait to the last second and get eliminated.

Guide.title: [E]: Binding Chain
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/binding-chain.png)Binding Chain

* ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki's most important dueling tool. Save your tether for enemies that get close to you, and are hard focusing on eliminating you. Bind them, and you’ll likely win the duel.

* Hinders and prevents movement abilities, like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/cassidy.png)Cassidy's grenade, and tethers to limit motion, like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mauga.png)Mauga's Ult. It’s not a hard stun; enemies can still attack while tethered.

* Blocked by barriers and deflect abilities. When using against a hero like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/genji.png)Genji, who can block the chain, wait until after you see them use deflect before trying to bind them.
* * Similar to Brig’s Flail, it is a ranged melee attack. Meaning it beats absorption abilities like Defense Matrix.
* Immediately binds to the ground beneath the target.

* * Example: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki can use Binding Chain against Jetpack Cat flying over the well in Illios, and Jetpack Cat will be pulled into the well. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki scores an environmental KO.

Guide.title: Ultimate: Kekkai Sanctuary
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/kekkai-sanctuary.png)Kekkai Sanctuary

* Not a barrier. The walls function the same as ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/d-va.png)D.Va's ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/defense-matrix.png)Defense Matrix. Blocks all projectiles.
* Does NOT block:
* * Beams
* Melee
* Shockwaves (Earth Shatter, D.Va Bomb, etc)

* Only the walls absorb projectiles. If the enemy enter inside the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/kekkai-sanctuary.png)Kekkai Sanctuary, they can shoot your team that is inside.
* When using at close range, stay near the perimeter so you can shield dance, and keep the enemy on the opposite side of the barrier from you, where they can’t shoot you.

Guide.title: Passive: Remedy Aura
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/remedy-aura.png)Remedy Aura
* Base AoE healing is abysmally low at 3.5 for self and 5 for allies. Dealing damage is the quickest way to gain aura charge (including damaging deployables). Healing abilities also charge the aura.
* Important to maintain a high charge for ult farming. Even though the max is 20 healing per second, that quickly adds up when you are grouped up with your team and healing multiple allies.

* Another reason why ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki wants to play offensively. The more damage he deals, the more he can passively heal his team.

Guide.title: Wellspring
content: * Helps keep your AoE healing higher and get it up sooner in fights.
* Good when your other Support lacks AoE healing.

Guide.title: Exposed Soul
content: * Considering enemies tethered by ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/binding-chain.png)Binding Chain can still attack you, it’s important to eliminate them as quickly as possible. Exposed Soul helps turn every successful chain into a KO.
* Best for duels and countering enemy dives.

Guide.title: Resonant Return
content: * To mazimize benefit of the extra bounce, try to use Healing Kasa when your team is positioned closely together.
* Good for increasing defensive capabilities.
* Best when you need to serve as the main source of your team’s sustain.

Guide.title: Quickstep
content: * Best for rush and dive comps, as it enables a hyper-aggressive team initiation.
* Similar to Lucio’s speed aura, communicating with your team via VC, ping, or a voice line like “3-2-1” is important for coordinating ability timings.
* * The speedboost window is short, so your team will get more benefit if they are prepared, instead of having to react once they realize the speed aura is active.

Guide.title: Maps
content: Maps that encourage close-range or brawly fights are the best for Mizuki to make full use of his kit (e.g., Oasis, Samoa, King's Row). Not only do these maps favor team comps he works well with, but they also allow him to get value from both his AoE healing and bouncing projectiles.

Long-range maps, such as Circuit Royal, and high-ground maps like Numbani are the two types of maps where ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki will struggle the most. As long as he can stay with his team, he can make it work, but he'll often feel at a disadvantage compared to other heroes.

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki has a hybrid kit that can adapt to multiple team comp styles. Ideally, he plays with rush comps where he can use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/katashiro-return.png)Katashiro Return to push up aggressively with a Tank like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/junker-queen.png)Junker Queen, then teleport back to safety.

Pairing him with a Support with high burst healing such as ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana makes for a great backline. They can use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/binding-chain.png)Binding Chain and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sleep-dart.png)Sleep Dart to protect themselves, while her burst healing and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/biotic-grenade.png)Biotic Grenade keeps the rest of their team alive.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: The best way to coutner ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki is to watch for his ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/katashiro-return.png)Katashiro Return animation, speed past him, and find his doll. If he TPs back to it, you get the kill. If he knows he can't go back, he likely overextended and is vulnerable to the rest of your team.

As a general strategy, remember that his healing is most effective when he is dealing damage. If possible, play outside of his primary fire range, and chip away at his team's health as he struggles to keep them alive.

During his ultimate, either full-commit or back away. When your team has melee heroes, go aggro, and you can kill through the healing. If your team is primarily projectiles, it's better to just wait out the 7-second duration before recommitting to the fight.

Guide.title: Overview
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/wuyang.png)Wuyang is a flexible Support hero who combines sustained healing, burst utility, and long-range damage into a single fluid kit. Trained in ancient water techniques, Wuyang approaches combat like the tide: steady when needed, or a huge wave of damage and healing when the moment is right. His mastery over water allows him to both mend allies and batter enemies, flowing seamlessly between protection and lethality.

In team compositions, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/wuyang.png)Wuyang functions as a frontline Support who plays closer to the action than most healers. He excels at enabling aggressive pushes, sustaining his Tank throughout the mid-fight, and providing burst healing in critical, fight-determining moments.

Guide.title: Play As
content: * Wait to use your Ult until you or your selected ally is right next to enemies, so it doesn’t expire before getting into attack range.
* Use Overflow to refill Wuyang’s healing resource while healing your Tank’s large health pool.
* Combine Guardian Wave with another Support’s AoE healing, such as Moira’s Biotic Orb.

Guide.title: Play Against
content: * When you see the ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/guardian-wave.png)Guardian Wave slam, back off, wait a few seconds, then hard re-engage to wipe his team because they won’t have burst healing.
* After you see him use Rushing Torrent (often to refill healing resources), immediately rush at him to eliminate Wuyang while he’s unable to escape.
* His Ult has a short 3.5s duration. Run away, use cover, and escape tools your hero has because it’s basically impossible to survive if you get caught.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Versatile Healer
* Sterrable Pojectile
* Good team fighting Ultimate
* Kit is pure utility
* Hard to hit abilities
* Limited escape options

Guide.title: Versatile Healing Options
content: Between ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/restorative-stream.png)Restorative Stream’s passive and active modes, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/guardian-wave.png)Guardian Wave’s healing amplification, and Tidal Blast’s burst heal, Wuyang has plenty of options to choose from when teammates are under fire.

Additionally, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/restorative-stream.png)Restorative Stream is one of just a handful of healing abilities that can heal through barriers, giving him the advantage in many scenarios.

Guide.title: Consistent Ranged Pressure
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/wuyang.png)Wuyang’s ranged damage is among the best in the Support class. Steering an orb blast to hit around corners is a unique strength that makes him a constant threat. While his damage potential is not quite as high as Zen’s, he offers much higher healing as a trade-off.

Guide.title: Fight Winning Ultimate
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/tidal-blast.png)Tidal Blast is one of the best Ults in the entire game. Overhealth, hard knockdown, burst healing all in one. Entire team fights can be won with just a well-timed Wuyang Ult.

Guide.title: Utility Focused Kit
content: Although this is technically one of his strengths, it’s also his weakness. To be a worthwhile pick, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/wuyang.png)Wuyang players must be able to manage their resources, read fights, track enemy positions, and know when to use his high value cooldowns. His abilities are really easy to waste and cause your team to lose the game.

Guide.title: Tricky Aim Mechanics
content: All the time you’ve spent clicking heads with hitscans won’t help you much when steering water orbs across the map. To be consistent with curving shots around corners requires a decent amount of time dedicated to this unique mechanic.

Guide.title: Limited Escape Options
content: Unlike the original iteration of ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/wuyang.png)Wuyang, which was way overtuned and nearly impossible to dive, the current version is vulnerable to dive enemies. One of the main ways he keeps his Tank alive is by using ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/rushing-torrent.png)Rushing Torrent with Overflow Perk to pump out more single-target healing. Doing this leaves him without an escape tool, so smart enemies will wait and punish him.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Xuanwu Staff
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/xuanwu-staff.png)Xuanwu Staff
* Water orbs need to travel about 8m before they can become empowered. When you are very close to your target, it is better to spam fire instead of trying to charge and control your shots.
* * Rapid firing at close range deals the same damage per orb, but the fire rate is significantly faster, resulting in much higher damage output.
* Empowered water orbs consume 2 ammo.

* Fully charged orbs deal more damage and can be guided. To min/max his damage per second, you can release them as soon as the charge completes and fire another volley. The orbs will slowly drop and spread out, so aim a bit high when doing this.
* Finish off low-health enemies around corners by curving orbs to hit enemies that are hiding out of your LoS.

Guide.title: Secondary Fire: Restorative Stream
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/restorative-stream.png)Restorative Stream
* Prioritize squishy allies, and especially those diving or taking up a lot of the enemy's attention.

* Treat ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/restorative-stream.png)Restorative Stream as primarily a passive ability. Set it and forget it. Focus on keeping your damage output high.
* Don’t spam target swapping.
* * Every time you heal with the beam, you trigger another 2-second delay before the healing resource refills itself.
* Remember to use your healing resource. Even though we just said not to get carried away with it, you still need to be very active with keeping allies healthy with your healing beam.
* * See an ally at half HP? Focus heal them.
* Both active and passive healing ignore barriers.
* * Typically, it is ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/wuyang.png)Wuyang's job to sustain aggressive allies pushing past enemy barriers

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Rushing Torrent
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/rushing-torrent.png)Rushing Torrent
* Grants a burst of speed followed by sustained mobility and increased jump height. Primarily, you should use it proactively to reposition to corners and high ground as your team moves around.
* Against teams with heavy dive or flank comps, always save this mobility tool and use it to escape their attack, or dash to a teammate for help.

Guide.title: [E]: Guardian Wave
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/guardian-wave.png)Guardian Wave
* Deals damage, heals allies, knocks enemies back, and increases healing received by 50% for 3 seconds.
* Best used once your team has taken a good amount of damage
* Don’t get baited into using it for a tiny bit of poke damage. Hitting an enemy Tank for 80 damage essentially does nothing.
* Good for finishing off enemies in close-range battles, especially if they are very mobile and difficult to hit with your primary fire.

Guide.title: Ultimate: Tidal Blast
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/tidal-blast.png)Tidal Blast
* Works best on aggressive, fast heroes diving into the enemy team. Always wait for your ally to be actively attack the enemy before giving them your ult.
* * Ping “Ult is Ready” to signal that you will assist them, so they know to be extra aggressive.

* Also works great as a tide shifter. When the enemy has committed multiple ultimates to try and eliminate your Tank, for example, you can keep them alive with overhealth and empower them to unleash a deadly counterattack.

Guide.title: Overflow
content: * Grants the ability to give more burst healing to your allies, and less offensive downtime for yourself due to less time spent reloading.
* Recommended Minor Perk

Guide.title: Balance
content: * Allows you to focus even more on dealing damage. As long as you keep hitting enemies, your selected ally will keep benefitting from increased healing.

Guide.title: Ebb and Flow
content: * Not a terrible perk, but not worth taking over Falling Rain.
* May help with countering dive comps by improving your close-range capabilities.
* Try it out if you have been unable to get value out of your charged primary fire up to this point.

Guide.title: Falling Rain
content: * Very powerful for increasing total and burst damage.
* As soon as you unlock the Major Perk, you should start putting more emphasis on dealing damage.
* All the same tips from ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/xuanwu-staff.png)Xuanwu Staff apply as the use case does not change.

Guide.title: Maps
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/wuyang.png)Wuyang has good horizontal and vertical mobility, long-range damage, and medium-range healing. These attributes allow him to adapt to most maps.
Regardless of the map, he wants to take advantage of his curving projectile to hit around corners, and jiggle peek cover to minimize his exposure to damage.

The maps he struggles most on are those with high ground areas that are outside his jump reach. Watchpoint: Gibraltar and Numbani, for example, have objective areas surrounded by high ground that Wuyang can't reach to contest or follow his team.
