Guide.title: Overview
content: An archaeologist by trade, Sloan Cameron brings their excavation tools to the battlefield! Known in game as ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/venture.png)Venture, their kit features a hybrid of melee and poke abilities. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/smart-excavator.png)SMART Excavator can be used for close range poke damage and is strong when holding tight choke points. Meanwhile, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/burrow.png)Burrow and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/drill-dash.png)Drill Dash are best utilized as close range flank tools.

Venture has to take a lot of high risks throughout a match, but when successful they are extremely disruptive to the enemy team's game plan. While their primary fire is technically a ranged ability, Venture will always want to try to keep their engagements within their melee range.

Guide.title: Play As
content: * Use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/burrow.png)Burrow and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/drill-dash.png)Drill Dash to close into melee range, since ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/venture.png)Venture excels at close-quarters flanks and burst combos rather than long-range poke.

* Manage your temporary shields from ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/explosive-resolve.png)Explosive Resolve by spacing out ability usage so you stay long enough to disengage.

* ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/tectonic-shock.png)Tectonic Shock is best used against heroes without vertical mobility as they struggle to escape the large ground pulses.

Guide.title: Play Against
content: * Venture can still be damaged after activating Burrow until their entire body is fully submerged. Don't let them get away!

* Make a mental note if you don't see ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/venture.png)Venture on your screen. They are likely setting up a flank attack, so be ready to counter.

* When they miss abilities, or you see them use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/drill-dash.png)Drill Dash and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/burrow.png)Burrow, that's your signal to hard-focus them at their most vulnerable.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Great at flanking
* Burst damage
* Disruption
* Gotta get in their face
* Easily countered
* All or nothing

Guide.title: Deep flanks
content: The shields generated by Explorer’s Resolve make Venture tanky enough to sustain focused damage on their own. Depending on the situation, Burrow and Drill Dash are interchangeable as engage/disengage abilities. Venture can use these abilities to position themselves behind the enemy backline. Once their cooldowns are back up, they can then go for an assassination. After flanking the enemy back line, Venture can escape over walls with Drill Dash or use Burrow’s invincibility to get out safely.

Guide.title: Burst damage
content: Primary fire, Burrow, and Tectonic Shock all provide great burst damage to players. Burst damage is even more important to OW heroes since the Armor rework in season 10. Moreover, many of Venture's abilities are cancellable into one another, enabling them to deal even faster and larger bursts of damage. (See combos under Tips and Tricks)

Guide.title: Disruption
content: Unlike many other heroes, Venture doesn’t have to get eliminations to be valuable for their team. When the enemy back line gets booped vertically by a Burrowed-Drill Dash, they have to keep an eye on Venture for an additional 4 seconds before they emerge. The time, focus and abilities dedicated to stopping Venture’s assassination is already extremely valuable. The crowd control from both Drill Dash can also disrupt enemy movement abilities and save Venture’s team from elimination.

Guide.title: Only useful at extremely close range
content: Venture’s primary fire is a slow moving projectile that can be difficult to direct impact at its max range of 16m. Their other three abilities have to be near melee range to deal damage at all. When against an enemy comp with lots of poke damage, Venture struggles to get in close enough to do damage and isn’t adding any value to their team until they do so.

Guide.title: Easily countered
content: Although Venture can be a very good flank hero, they are also easily and heavily countered. Burrow’s long cast animation doesn’t grant invulnerability until completely submerged. CC abilities like Sleep Dart and Magnetic Grenade basically make Burrow unusable as an escape ability.

Guide.title: All or nothing
content: Because Venture’s best damaging abilities are also their escape abilities, Venture often has to go in and use every resource to secure an elimination, leaving them completely vulnerable to a counterattack. Venture caught without either Burrow or Drill Dash is a sitting duck and has no counter play if focused by the enemy team.

Guide.title: [Primary Fire]: Smart Excavator
content: Tips for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/smart-excavator.png)SMART Excavator
* Take advantage of its AoE damage to farm ultimate against grouped enemies.
* Taking a slight off-angle allows Venture to stay with their team while also keeping themselves in range for Primary Fire.
* Decent spam ability when holding a choke point.

Guide.title: [Secondary Fire]: Drill Dash
content: Tips for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/drill-dash.png)Drill Dash
* Equally good for movement and damage.
* When flanking, Drill Dash should typically be saved to ensure a safe escape.

* Prevent enemy escapes by knocking them around with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/drill-dash.png)Drill Dash. This is especially lethal if you get behind them and push them into your teammates.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Burrow
content: Tips for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/burrow.png)Burrow
* Never use Burrow near an enemy with a strong CC ability (e.g., Sleep Dart, Flashbang) unless you are certain it is on cooldown.
* Whenever possible, begin engagements with Burrow.
* Position between multiple enemies to maximize AoE damage output.
* Drill Dashing immediately after fully submerging will fully refill the cooldown upon emergence if the entire 4 seconds of Burrow are used.
* Venture can still be damaged after activating Burrow until their entire body is fully submerged, which makes it unreliable as a quick escape tool compared to Moira’s Fade or Reaper’s Wraith Form.

Guide.title: [Melee] Clobber
content: Tips for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/clobber.png)Clobber
* Can cancel into Clobber out of Primary Fire.
* Can cancel at any point during the drilling animation into Drill Dash or Burrow.
* The full 70 damage goes through barriers such as Reinhardt’s Barrier Field.

Guide.title: [Ultimate]: Tectonic Shock
content: * Blocked by barriers, so first rule is to track when the enemy has barriers available or how much barrier HP they have.
* Best when used on a flank unexpectedly.
* Target squishies and avoid Tanks.
* 75 HP of shield health lasts for the entire duration of the ultimate plus 3 seconds before decay begins, giving Venture an effective 325 HP while ulting.
* * Bonus health can be repeatedly healed by Supports.

Guide.title: “One-shot” Combos
content: (All assume direct impact with Primary Fire.)

* ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/smart-excavator.png)SMART Excavator → Melee → ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/drill-dash.png)Drill Dash
Fastest burst of damage. Deals a near-instantaneous 195 damage.

* ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/smart-excavator.png)SMART Excavator → ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/drill-dash.png)Drill Dash → ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/smart-excavator.png)SMART Excavator → Melee
* * Most reliable combo.

* Eliminates all non-Tank heroes except ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/bastion.png)Bastion and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/torbjorn.png)Torbjörn.
* Burrow (max damage) → Primary Fire → Primary Fire (Drill Dash to escape)
* * Kills 250 HP and below heroes.

Guide.title: Deep Burrow
content: * Good for flanks and increasing overall mobility.
* Enables more efficient engages and disengages.

Guide.title: Excavation Exhilaration
content: * You dump all your cooldowns to get in and weaken enemies, pop ult, and quickly get them all back.
* The best part is you can burrow into Ult and then again to escape.

Guide.title: Smart Extender
content: * Really good to give yourself some poke potential.
* Best use is to finish off elims on targets who escape your range mid-fight.
* Though brief, it’s nice to have an option for better ranged damage.

Guide.title: Covered in Dirt
content: * Best for general flank and close-range combat playstyle that Venture primarily sticks to. Makes them more tanky during fights.

Guide.title: Ilios Well
content: * Ilios Well provides Venture with plenty of walls and high ground to safely escape to. While Venture does terrible in the open area around the Well, both sides of the map are great for setting up flank routes. Both sides of the point also have walls Venture can jump over with either Burrow or Drill Dash.

Guide.title: Oasis City Center
content: * The objective point on City Center has natural cover for Venture to circumnavigate even if both of their abilities are on cooldown. Additionally, the side routes all have health packs and safe areas to engage from or escape to.

Guide.title: Hollywood
content: * Venture has to create flank routes to be effective on Hollywood and adapt to where the enemy team is positioned. On this map, the backlines often set up well behind their front line. The space offers the perfect opportunity for Venture to embark on its own solo mission to disrupt or eliminate the separated enemy blackline.

Guide.title: Havana
content: * Havana tends to be one of the worst maps for all close range heroes. Not only are the map areas incredibly wide and open, but most areas also lack usable cover for Venture.

Guide.title: Junker Town
content: * Poke positions and high ground are incredibly strong on Junker Town. Venture struggles to stage and find pathing to ever reach their optimal attack range.

Guide.title: New Queen Street
content: * The initial robot starting area on New Queen Street is doable for Venture, since they can use the high-ground tunnel and the mega health pack room. The final points on either side of the map are just way too open for Venture. They become dependent upon their team's resources to stay alive and be effective.

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: Venture works best in Brawl Comps that can utilize their close range damage.
**Ideal team comp built around Venture:**

![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mauga.png)Mauga, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/venture.png)Venture, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/cassidy.png)Cassidy, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/kiriko.png)Kiriko, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/lifeweaver.png)Lifeweaver

Guide.title: Individual synergies with other heroes
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mauga.png)Mauga

* The synergy between Mauga and Venture revolves entirely around Cardiac Overdrive usage. Pairing Cardiac Overdrive’s damage reduction and life steal with the Venture’s shield hp generation makes for a deadly combo. Venture becomes virtually unkillable for the 5 seconds they are buffed by Mauga. Furthermore, Mauga can coordinate Overrun and slam with Venture’s engages and Cage Fight leaves caught enemies nowhere to run from Tectonic Shock.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sombra.png)Sombra

* Sombra is the easiest hero to follow Venture’s flanks with and Hack can prevent enemies from using CC on Venture. The amount of resources it takes from a team just to survive a Sombra/Venture dive also gives the rest of your team a huge window of opportunity to go aggressive.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/lifeweaver.png)Lifeweaver

* Venture can struggle to both confirm an elim and still have the resources to safely escape. Life Grip allows Venture to dump all of their cooldowns into the enemy and be pulled to safety. This combo can be extremely difficult for enemy teams to stop and can typically be cycled every other time Venture engages.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: Unfortunately for Venture, they are actually one of the easiest heroes in OW to counter. The long cast time of Burrow gives time for teams to focus fire to death before the invulnerability kicks in. Simply choosing one of the counter picks below is typically enough to shut down Ventures. In general, pinging the Venture when they begin their engagement will prevent many deaths. Always try to track where the Venture player approaches from and learn their escape patterns so you can follow up and eliminate them before regrouping with your team.

Guide.title: Specific Hero Counters
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/doomfist.png)Doomfist

* Doomfist’s mobility outclasses Venture’s and allows him to hunt Venture down where they would normally be safe. Rocket Punch cancels Burrow and guarantees death. The multiple burst damage abilities of Venture also gives easy charge to Doomfist for his Empowered Punch.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/cassidy.png)Cassidy
* Magnetic Grenade. Even if you have horrible aim with Cassidy, all you need to do is stick them with a Magnetic Grenade and your team can easily follow up with enough damage to elim her.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana

* Similar to Magnetic Grenade, Sleep Dart hard counters Venture’s game plan and abilities. The brief moment of slow movement and vulnerability during the startup frames of Burrow is the easiest opportunity for Ana land a sleep.

Guide.title: Specific Hero Counters names
content: doomfist
cassidy
ana

Guide.title: Overview
content: The dual shotgun-wielding and ruthless killer who haunts the nightmares of tank mains. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/reaper.png)Reaper has the very specific role of the point-blank combatant. At medium to long ranges, he provides almost zero value to his team. If he manages to get right in the enemy's face, he’ll instantly have the upper hand.

His must be disciplined to have the patience required to set up sneaky flanks and avoid damage on their way to their target. He’s equally effective at quickly eliminating isolated enemies and going toe-to-toe with tanks. Depending on the map and match-ups, he can adapt his target prioritization and take out the most vulnerable enemy.

Guide.title: Play As
content: * Look for isolated enemies in the backlines. They’ll be the easiest to eliminate and can quickly give your team the advantage.

* Save ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/wraith-form.png)Wraith Form to survive. Try to sneak in and attack, then only use Wraith once at low HP and needing to escape.
* Help your Tank win the Tank duel. Especially in Tank Mirrors, the extra damage from Reaper gives your Tank an easy win when fighting the enemy Tank.

Guide.title: Play Against
content: * Focus him after Wraith. Even if you have to chase after him, a Reaper without ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/wraith-form.png)Wraith Form is an easy kill.

* Listen for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/shadow-step.png)Shadow Step sound cue. Whichever direction you hear it from tells you he’s about to appear and attack you.

* Counter ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/death-blossom.png)Death Blossom with CC, damage mitigation, or focus fire. He’s moving slowly and can’t cancel Blossom, so he’s easy to target.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Tank buster
* Backline assassin
* Self-reliant
* Poor range
* Ult is easy to counter
* Armor

Guide.title: Tank buster
content: The wide bullet spread of Reaper’s Shotguns is perfect for shooting the large bodies of Tanks. They also serve as a large source of lifesteal health for himself. Between the high damage and lifesteal, most Tanks try to avoid Reaper at all costs.

Guide.title: Backline assassin
content: Shadow Step and Wraith Form are great flanking tools. Reaper can TP behind the enemy, surprise attack, secure an elim, then turn invincible and escape.

Guide.title: Self-reliant
content: Having life steal, mobility, and invincibility means Reaper doesn’t have to rely on his team’s resources. He’s a great hero to pick when you feel your team isn’t providing enough support. Between health packs and lifesteal, Reaper can keep his HP full all on his own.

Guide.title: Poor range
content: His only attack, being the Hellfire Shotguns with short falloff and wide bulletspread, doesn’t permit Reaper to find value outside of very close range. During poke phases, Reaper doesn’t do anything. Getting in close also puts himself in greater danger.

Guide.title: Easily countered ult
content: In Overwatch 2, ults are seen as game-changing abilities. Sadly for Reaper, however, his ult is difficult to get consistent value out of. The timing of the ult tends to be telegraphed, and there are endless ways to counter it, from damage mitigation and invincibility to stuns and burst damage.

Guide.title: Armor
content: Armor reduces Reaper's shotgun damage by half. So if he’s shooting a Tank with high amounts of armor like Orisa, he’s dealing very low damage until he and his team chip away down to her base health.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Hellfire Shotguns
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/hellfire-shotguns.png)Hellfire Shotguns
* Up close and personal
* * Hellfire Shotguns’ damage scales way up when at extreme close ranges. At just 10 meters away, the falloff damage kicks in, and the bullet spread causes a lot of pellets to miss.
* Barrel stuffing enemies ensures the maximum amount of Shotgun pellets hit, which leads to more damage and more lifesteal.
* Reaper has the advantage in virtually every duel when at 5m or closer.
* Critical hits

* * One headshot plus one body shot instantly eliminates all DPS and Supports. (assuming close range and all pellets hit). Going for headshots with Reaper is extremely important, as he relies on the burst damage to quickly kill and escape before he dies. The close-range engagements also make headshotting more reliable compared to heroes who play at longer ranges.
* Trigger discipline
* * One shot every half second sounds pretty fast, but when targeting fast and small enemies like Juno, try to individually trigger each shot. You’ll save ammo and improve accuracy.

* Additionally, wait to fire until you are at very close range when sneaking up on an enemy who doesn’t see you. Don’t shoot the moment you see someone if they don’t see you. That way you maximize your advantage in the fight.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Wraith Form
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/wraith-form.png)Wraith Form
* Use for invincibility

* * The primary use for Wraith Form should be survival. In an ideal world, Reaper players would always engage without needing to use Wraith Form, and then be able to use it to safely escape when at low health.
* If you use Wraith Form to get close to your target, Reaper becomes a sitting duck if the enemy team turns to focus him.
* Use for reloading

* * Activating and instantly cancelling Wraith Form will quickly reload a full clip and help Reaper to confirm elims on targets with low HP. Oftentimes, you will find yourself in a scenario where you’re out of ammo and your target just barely lives. Wraith Form reload cancel will help you get those elims.

* Important to remember. On the occasions where you don’t save Wraith Form, be sure to plan out how you will survive. Is there cover nearby? Health packs? Healing or damage mitigation resources? Knowing the answers to these will enable you to play more aggressively.

Guide.title: [E]: Shadow Step
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/shadow-step.png)Shadow Step
* Loud sound cue

* * First and foremost, you need to know that when Reaper arrives at his selected teleport location, he makes a loud sound that nearby enemies can hear. Be prepared for their reaction when Shadow Stepping close to enemies, even if it's behind a wall.
* Use to set up flanks
* * Shadow Step is good for getting behind or above the enemy. Then, crouch walk right up to them without them noticing Reaper. Doing this will teach enemy backlines to fear the Reaper
* Never TP in enemy LoS

* * Reaper is a motionless target when activating Shadow Step and when arriving at the selected point. If he’s in enemy LoS for either of these, they get free headshots and often have enough time to kill him before he can move or use Wraith Form.

Guide.title: Ultimate: Death Blossom
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/death-blossom.png)Death Blossom
* Be sneaky

* * To increase your elims and success with Death Blossom, focus on catching the enemy off guard. If they don’t see Reaper, then are suddenly being attacked by Death Blossom from behind, they have much less time to react.
* Don’t Wraith Form into Blossom

* * Reapers everywhere love to do it. So much so that enemies are trained to expect Death Blossom any time they see Reaper Wraith Form into their team. Doing so will likely get you hacked, stunned, or have the ult blocked, ultimately ending in the death of Reaper.
* Finish off targets
* * Death Blossom auto locks onto all enemies and deployables within its AoE. This is useful for finishing off targets if you run out of ammo, or are having difficulty landing the final blow.

Guide.title: (Passive) The Reaping
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/the-reaping.png)The Reaping
* 30% Lifesteal
* * All damage Reaper deals with his Shotguns, including during Death Blossom, heals Reaper.
* When at low HP with no escape, focus on shooting Tanks or low mobility enemies who you are more likely to quickly deal damage to. In doing so, you’ll generate self-healing more quickly.
* Pay close attention to your health
* * During fights, Reaper’s health constantly goes up and down from healing and damage. Be sure to watch your HP bar to know when you need to Wraith Form to survive.

Guide.title: Lingering Wraith
content: * Extra tanky
* * Soul Globes are useful for making Reaper even more tanky with the added self-sustain. Allow him to stay in the fight a bit longer.
* Especially good in brawly fights on the objectives where enemies are dying in close range.
* Don’t try to pick up every Globe

* * Just because you see a Globe doesn’t mean you should pick it up. They can be bait and waste time for very little healing in return. Only pick them up when at critical health or when they are on the path to your targeted enemy.
Lingering Wraith
* Dangerous Perk

* * The speed boost encourages using ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/wraith-form.png)Wraith Form to engage, but then you don't have it to escape. You need to be extremely confident you will get the elim, and still survive.
* Useful against mobile targets whose mobility lasts longer or moves them farther than your Wraith Form.

Guide.title: Soul Reaving
content: * Extra tanky
* * Soul Globes are useful for making Reaper even more tanky with the added self-sustain. Allow him to stay in the fight a bit longer.
* Especially good in brawly fights on the objectives where enemies are dying in close range.
* Don’t try to pick up every Globe

* * Just because you see a Globe doesn’t mean you should pick it up. They can be bait and waste time for very little healing in return. Only pick them up when at critical health or when they are on the path to your targeted enemy.
Lingering Wraith
* Dangerous Perk

* * The speed boost encourages using ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/wraith-form.png)Wraith Form to engage, but then you don't have it to escape. You need to be extremely confident you will get the elim, and still survive.
* Useful against mobile targets whose mobility lasts longer or moves them farther than your Wraith Form.

Guide.title: Dire Triggers
content: * Poke weapon
* * Greatly increased range damage and tightened bullet spread empower Reaper to finally be able to contribute to ranged fights.
* Before getting in close, start building ult charge, or pressuring the enemy team.
* Help with fliers

* * In matches with fliers like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/pharah.png)Pharah or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/echo.png)Echo, Dire Triggers' longer range helps to pressure or even finish them off.
* Don’t give away your position on flanks

* * The damage from Dire Triggers isn’t worth beginning your flank attacks with. It’s still much better to get as close as possible, then attack with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/hellfire-shotguns.png)Hellfire Shotguns.

Guide.title: Shadow Blink
content: * Enables safer escape with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/shadow-step.png)Shadow Step. The best use of the faster cast time is being able to get out of fights when you don't have ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/wraith-form.png)Wraith Form.
* Recommended if you are using Lingering Wraith

Guide.title: Maps
content: Reaper thrives on maps with tight spaces and lots of small rooms. He struggles most on maps with long sightlines, narrow hallways, and wide open spaces. Finding areas with cover and flank routes should be the primary focus of your pathing on Reaper. If one side of the objective has health packs or covered paths, spend most of your time on that side and avoid the other. Maps with high ground areas give him the extra option to TP up, then drop down for a lethal surprise attack.

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: Reaper's best ally is ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/zarya.png)Zarya because of ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/projected-barrier.png)Projected Barrier and her frontline presence.

When he dives in and gets bubbled, he has a couple seconds to delete the enemy without fear of getting stunned. Likewise, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/projected-barrier.png)Projected Barrier is a great tool for enabling high-value ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/death-blossom.png)Death Blossoms.

He also works well with other brawl and rush Tanks, can dive with the mobile Tanks, but gets little value from poke Tanks like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/domina.png)Domina and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sigma.png)Sigma.

Since he needs to be up close and personal, Supports who can heal him while he's in the enemy backline are the best choices. A couple examples are ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/lifeweaver.png)Lifeweaver who can heal, and save Reaper with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/life-grip.png)Life Grip when needed. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana can bust heal, anti-![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/biotic-grenade.png)Biotic Grenade for kills, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/nano-boost.png)Nano Boost for an ultra deadly Reaper attack.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: The strongest playstyle for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/reaper.png)Reaper to carry his team with is a flanker who assassinates backline heroes like Supports and Snipers. This is the main thing you need to stop. He's also good when brawling Tanks, but outside of these two scenarios, his usefulness is very limited. Your job is to make both of these as difficult for him as possible.
First off, almost every hero has better range than him so focus on staying outside of his range where you can attack him before he gets into close range.

Listen for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/shadow-step.png)Shadow Step sound cue. Whichever direction you hear it from tells you he’s about to appear and attack you. Same goes for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/wraith-form.png)Wraith Form, if you see him use it towards you, immediately use your mobility to get away.

Save your knockback or stuns for after he's used Wraith whenever possible. Also very important is to focus him after Wraith, even if you have to chase after him, because a Reaper without ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/wraith-form.png)Wraith Form is an easy kill.

Counter ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/death-blossom.png)Death Blossom with CC, damage mitigation, or focus fire. He’s moving slowly and can’t cancel Blossom, so he’s easy to target.

Guide.title: Overview
content: Specialising in controlling space and manipulating the environment, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mei.png)Mei’s opponents end up frozen with fear.

![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/ice-wall.png)Ice Wall defines her kit and has ruined the day for countless Tank mains. Against heroes with poor mobility, getting walled off can feel like a helpless situation with no counterplay. Don’t sleep on her at long ranges either, because her icicle secondary fire can two-tap you from across the map.
Typically, Mei will position pushed up with her Tank where she has the most opportunities to split off the enemy team. Once she gets her Perks activated, be ready to deal with constant crowd control.

Guide.title: Play As
content: * Isolate the enemy Tank from their team by placing ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/ice-wall.png)Ice Wall right behind them.

* When Ice Wall and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/cryo-freeze.png)Cryo-Freeze are both on cooldown, stay near your allies and away from the enemy.
* Use Ice Wall as a shield to protect yourself. It’s great for cutting off enemy LoS and keeping you and your team safe.

Guide.title: Play Against
content: * Break her wall! Shoot a single pillar to quickly create an opening for trapped teammates to walk through.

* Play around her cooldowns. When she has ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/ice-wall.png)Ice Wall, don’t casually walk through a choke and get walled off. Wait until she’s used it before pushing up.
* Stay outside her primary fire range. Her secondary fire range is less consistent and easier to deal with.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Divide and conquer
* Controller
* Good kit
* Feast or famine
* Low damage
* Immobile

Guide.title: Divide and conquer
content: The main reason to pick Mei is for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/ice-wall.png)Ice Wall. Splitting off enemies from their team is often the quickest and most consistent way to win fights.

Guide.title: Controls space
content: Mei’s presence and threat of Ice Wall are good for holding choke points and controlling areas. Anytime the enemy wants to get close, they’ll have to plan how to survive her primary fire, Ice Wall, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/blizzard.png)Blizzard.

Guide.title: Adaptable kit
content: She can be a frontliner, ranged poke, and an anti-dive hero. Mei’s kit allows her to adapt to what her team needs based on team comps and map selection.

Guide.title: Feast or Famine
content: Abilities like Ice Wall, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/blizzard.png)Blizzard, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/endothermic-blaster.png)Endothermic Blaster are either massive value or zero value. A poorly placed Ice Wall does nothing, and if you can’t hit secondary fire consistently, you’re contributing nothing to the fight.

Guide.title: Low damage
content: Damage output is not her strong suit. Sometimes this leads to slow Ult building and falling behind in Ult economy. If you aren’t getting elims from Ice Wall, you should probably swap off Mei.

Guide.title: No mobility
content: Other than using Ice Wall as an elevator, Mei has no mobility whatsoever. She can protect herself, but she can’t escape, reposition quickly, or chase down retreating enemies.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Endothermic Blaster
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/endothermic-blaster.png)Endothermic Blaster
* Slow enemy retreats

* * The slow debuff increases the amount of time it takes for enemies to disengage from the fight. If you see an enemy trying to escape, keep primary fire on them and buy your team more time to eliminate them.
* Slow then icicle
* * For increased burst damage, once you’ve inflicted slow on the enemy, try to headshot them with secondary fire.
* Treated as a beam weapon
* * Endothermic Blaster ignores Defense Matrix, Deflect, Javelin Spin, and Kinetic Grasp. When you see these abilities used, you can damage the hero through it.

Guide.title: Secondary Fire: Endothermic Blaster Icicle
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/endothermic-blaster.png)Endothermic Blaster
* Poke
* * Mei has decent poke capabilities. Landing a single critical hit with icicle on any DPS or Support forces them to hide and wait for healing.
* In the beginning phases of a fight, use secondary fire to build ult charge, and possibly get an early pick.
* Hold angles
* * Icicle’s slow rate of fire makes it good for jiggle peeking. Stand at a corner or wall and try to only expose yourself when firing. Then, quickly hide behind cover between each shot.
* Headshot frozen enemies
* * Anytime you freeze an enemy with Blizzard or Deep Freeze, always headshot them with secondary fire. Don’t keep holding primary fire because the damage is significantly lower.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Cryo-Freeze
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/cryo-freeze.png)Cryo-Freeze
* Invincibility
* * Counters stun. In match-ups against enemies with stuns like Cassidy Flashbang or Ana’s Sleep Dart, use Cryo-Freeze to block their stun. Doing so essentially guarantees you’ll win the duel.
* Mei takes zero damage from enemy attacks and can’t be healed by allies in Cryo-Freeze. Useful to survive attacks you otherwise couldn’t escape, like Gravitic Flux.
* Breaks LoS
* * Earth Shatter, D.Va bomb, and Deadeye are all good examples of Ultimates that require LoS. Ice blocking not only protects you, but it can also shield a teammate hiding directly behind you.
* Reloads Endothermic Blaster
* * While in ice block, Mei slowly reloads about half her ammo.
* Healing
* * A full duration Cryo-Freeze will restore Mei’s entire health.
* Block doors
* * When your team is capturing an objective, and the enemy team is returning from their spawn, Cryo-Freeze in small doorways to block their path for five seconds.
* They can’t do anything to stop you, and can Ice Wall after for increased safety and stall duration.

Guide.title: [E]: Ice Wall
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/ice-wall.png)Ice Wall
* Wall Tanks

* * Easiest way to quickly win a fight is to separate a Tank from the rest of their team by placing Ice Wall directly behind the Tank. They’ll be cut off from healing, and their team can’t attack yours. Unless the Tank can jump over the Wall, they typically won’t survive.
* Wall choke points
* * Whether you are stalling the objective and want to stop the entire team from entering, or dividing the team in half, chokes are Mei’s best friend.
* Even leaving a single enemy stuck behind Ice Wall gives your team the opportunity to win while you are one player up.
* Cut off LoS
* * Ice Wall breaks LoS from any abilities that require LoS. You can Wall in front of Immortality Field to prevent its effect.
* Ults like Earth Shatter and Annihilation can be blocked by Ice Wall.
* Rotations
* * If the enemy team has the poke advantage, Wall them off to buy your team time to rotate across open.
* Trap enemies in a 1v1
* * Mei is really good in close-range 1v1 because her primary fire is easy to hit, slows the enemy, and she can heal herself. Anytime an enemy ends up in a room with you, Wall the exit to trap them.
* Stall objectives
* * Of all the DPS, Mei is the best at stalling objectives. Go into a corner and Ice Wall yourself while waiting for your team to return.
* Coming out of Cryo-Freeze, look straight down and Ice Wall. You’ll end up on top and can jump down to separate yourself from the enemy waiting to attack you.
* Ice elevator.
* * Ice wall beneath your feet and you’ll lift up yourself and nearby allies. Useful for accessing high ground for yourself and other teammates who have no vertical mobility.

Guide.title: Ultimate: Blizzard
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/blizzard.png)Blizzard
* Trap with Wall
* * Place an Ice Wall just behind the enemy as they try to escape your Ult.
* Blizzard freeze effect goes through your Wall, so don’t worry about cutting off your LoS.
* Survive with Cryo-Freeze
* * If you go deep into the enemy team for Blizzard, you can Cryo-Freeze until the enemy freezes, then exit and start right-clicking their heads.
* Primary fire speeds up the freeze effect
* * Shooting enemies with primary fire will freeze them from Blizzard quicker.
* Needs LoS
* * Walls, structures, and Lifeweaver Tree cut off Blizzard’s AoE.
* Blizzard does, however, go through shields and barriers.
* Cast time
* * After a short startup animation, Mei tosses the Blizzard drone, but it only activates once it’s landed on the ground.
* Against D.Va and Sigma specifically, throw straight at the ground or in between their absorption abilities.
* Wait out mobility and invulnerability

* * Against enemies with dashes or CC immune abilities like Fortify, wait until you see those abilities used before using Blizzard. Otherwise, they will easily counter your ult, and you’ll have wasted it.

Guide.title: Skating Rink
content: * Adds a defensive benefit to your Ult.

* Even if half the enemy team is not frozen and can shoot you, you can wall them, heal up yourself and your team while eliminating the enemies that are frozen. Then you have an easy clean up against those left.

* Good for survivine damage over time and so you don't have to spend so much time in ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/cryo-freeze.png)Cryo-Freeze during your ult.

Guide.title: Glacial Propulsion
content: * Best use is for taking and contesting high ground areas.
* Has a low maximum height, so you can't jump off high ground and activate it to get an extra boost.

* Especially good on high maps with a bit of high ground like King's Row and Blizzard World where ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mei.png)Mei normally has a weakness against heroes with vertical mobility.

Guide.title: Deep Freeze
content: * Play close and hold corners
* * The ability to freeze enemies means you’ll want to spend as much time in primary fire range as possible. Position up front with your tank, or find enemies you can flank.
* When defending, stay at the choke and any corners. This forces close-range fights. Anyone who approaches you has to deal with the threat of being frozen, on top of getting walled off.
* Anti-Dive
* * Freezing any dive DPS is a death sentence for them. When the enemy team has mobility heroes giving you a hard time, shut them down with the Deep Freeze.

Guide.title: Cryo-Storm
content: * Big damage potential
* * Cryo-Storm deals 70 damage every second for up to 350 damage total.
* Try to trap an enemy in a corner or between Ice Wall and Cryo-storm.
* Block doorways
* * As noted in the Cryo-Freeze tips, blocking doorways is very strong for capturing and stalling objectives. Cryo-Storm adds damage as well, making the tactic even better!
* Ult charge
* * The extra damage Mei deals from Cryo-Storm adds up to a lot of extra ult generation over the course of a game. This is especially true when getting multiple enemies in your AoE.
* Blizzard combo
* * Similar to your primary fire, the slow effect of Cryo-Storm will speed up the freeze effect of Blizzard.
* The tech is OP since Mei’s invincible and slows enemies too fast for them to escape by walking out.

Guide.title: Maps
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mei.png)Mei tends to have an easier time finding value on non-payload maps. The stationary objectives of Control, Flashpoint, and Clash naturally have chokepoints for Mei to Wall off.

Regardless of the game mode, Mei likes maps with tight spaces and wants to avoid wide open spaces at all costs. Icicle gives her decent poke pressure, but she’s at a clear disadvantage against snipers on long sight lines. Since she lacks mobility, she also struggles on maps that favor dive and have a lot of high ground.

Guide.title: Watchpoint
content: Gibraltar

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: The biggest component of a team composition that helps ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mei.png)Mei perform well is a strong frontline. Because she has limited range on her primary fire and wall, she wants her Tank to hold the front, so she can safely push up with them. Tanks like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/reinhardt.png)Reinhardt, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/orisa.png)Orisa and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/domina.png)Domina all do this job well.

Also, when she uses ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/ice-wall.png)Ice Wall to split off the enemy, each of these can slam the enemy into the wall for a quick kill before the enemy has a chance to break wall.

For the rest of the team, it's mostly based on map and the enemy team comp. If they have fliers, she wants a hitscan as the other DPS, if the enemy is running dives, she wants Supports who can escape the dive on their own.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: The way ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mei.png)Mei wins game is by splitting off your team with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/ice-wall.png)Ice Wall. To counter Mei, you need to nullify the value her walls get.

First off, if you are the Tank, try to bait out walls. When you know Mei is waiting for you to walk through a choke point to wall and kill you, strafe forward and back. This will throw off her timing and you can end up on the safe side of the wall. Then, you should push in aggressively before the cooldown refreshes.
In general, try to stay outside her primary fire range. Her secondary fire range is less consistent and easier to deal with, but if you're getting frozen, it's difficult to win.

Guide.title: Specific Hero Counters names
content: ashe
hanzo
widowmaker
sojourn

Guide.title: Overview
content: Widowmaker is the purest expression of mechanical skill in Overwatch. A cold, methodical sniper conditioned to eliminate targets without hesitation. She is the most feast or famine hero in the game, but players with high precision can carry just about any team.

In team compositions, Widowmaker serves as an area control DPS. She doesn’t brawl, dive, or frontline. Instead, she threatens instant death and makes a simple move like walking around a corner a life-or-death decision. A single pick can decide the fight before it even begins.
While even missed shots can deny space, slow pushes, get out cooldowns, Widowmaker only gets value when she forces the enemy team to respect her sightlines by getting a few early insta-kills.
Although she has the potential to be the most lethal hero, she collapses quickly when the enemy prevents her from setting up or dives her from multiple angles.

Guide.title: Play As
content: * Hold long sightlines. Widow is at her strongest when she positions outside everyone else’s effective range, where she can still one-shot.
* Reposition frequently after shots. Don’t stay in one spot for long because the enemy will flank you and take you out.
* Prioritize pressure and picks over raw damage numbers. Don’t worry about total damage on the scoreboard. The only thing that matters is shutting down the enemy team, and getting solo kills.

Guide.title: Play Against
content: * Force her to retreat with dives and flanks. Even if you don’t get the kill, stop her from aiming at your teammates.
* Never peek the same angle twice. If you see Widow aiming down sights, don’t walk out at the same position because she will be ready to hit the shot.
* Avoid her sightlines. Scout or get info from your team about her position. Then take side routes where she can’t snipe you.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Instant oneshot potential
* Good lane control
* Solo carry hero
* Feast or famine
* Vulnerable against dive
* Underwhelming Ultimate

Guide.title: Instant oneshots
content: Widowmaker can delete squishy heroes with a single fully charged headshot, instantly giving her team the numbers advantage. At that point, her team will generally win the 5v4.

Guide.title: Lane control
content: Her presence alone denies open areas and long hallways. This forces enemies to take slower side routes, rely on barriers, or burn mobility cooldowns.

Guide.title: Solo carry potential
content: If you are cracked and think your team is holding you back, there is no better solo carry than Widowmaker. The better your aim, positioning, and target selection, the more oppressive she becomes.

Guide.title: Feast or famine
content: You either click heads and win, or miss shots and lose. There’s not really an in-between. Widow offers little consistent damage compared to other DPS if she isn’t deleting full HP squishies.

Guide.title: Highly vulnerable to dive
content: Grappling Hook is on a 10-second cooldown, which is longer than most dive heroes' mobility cooldowns. Even if she escapes their initial attack, they can chase after her and get the kill before she has another Grappling Hook.

Guide.title: Underwhelming DPS Ult
content: Wall hacks aren’t a bad Ult for a sniper hero to have, and it does force the enemy team to position extremely cautiously for its duration. However, compared to other DPS Ults like Sojourn’s Overclock, it’s not exactly a win-button.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Widow’s Kiss (SMG)
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/widows-kiss.png)Widow's Kiss
* Use unscoped fire only at close range or to finish off very low-health targets.
* Never rely on this mode in extended fights because you’ll just waste ammo. It’s a last resort, not a go-to strategy.

Guide.title: Secondary Fire: Widow's Kiss (ADS)
content: **Tips for Secondary Fire:** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/widows-kiss.png)Widow's Kiss (ADS)
* Fully charged shots deal 300 damage. You don’t need to fully charge if your target has lower health.
* Be patient, line up the shot, and avoid panic firing.
* Body shots to finish low targets are more consistent. Headshots are not always needed.
* Fire a few shots, then reposition. You want to be as unpredictable as possible. If an enemy doesn’t know where you are and that you are aiming at them, they are much easier to shoot.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Grappling Hook
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/grappling-hook.png)Grappling Hook
* Jump shots are awesome, but don’t let your ego cause you a bunch of deaths. Smart enemies will see you fly through the air, then immediately dive you, knowing you can’t escape.
* Use Grapple primarily for repositioning. Take high ground and off angles whenever possible.
* Pre-plan grapple spots so you can quickly take new angles or escape the moment you see an enemy trying to flank you.

Guide.title: [E]: Venom Mine
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/venom-mine.png)Venom Mine
* Place mines on common flank routes, staircases, or behind you. Even if the enemy sees it and destroys it, the information that an enemy is there is invaluable.
* For example, placing a Venom Mine to guard the only route to attack you on the left side means you will only need to watch out for enemies on your right side.
* Don’t forget to replace it when moving to a new position.

Guide.title: Ultimate: Infra-Sight
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/infra-sight.png)Infra-Sight

* Provides full enemy vision to your entire team. Your Ult is a teamfight utility. It’s better to stay alive the full duration and let your team benefit than to make an extremely dangerous and desperate attempt for a kill.
* Best used before a fight begins to enable safe pushes and give yourself and your team the advantage in setup.
* Watch for enemies to peek and shoot them the moment they enter your LoS

She makes good use of barriers by standing behind their cover and sniping without fear of getting picked off herself. This also benefits the Tank because the threat of getting one-shot by Widow reduces pressure on their barrier as well.

Another helpful archetype are heores with strong coutner-dive kits such as ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/torbjorn.png)Torbjörn or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/lucio.png)Lúcio who can peel for Widow. Anyone who can can CC or put high damage pressure on flankers and dive enemies will increase her odds of surviving, even if she's already used ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/grappling-hook.png)Grappling Hook.

Overall, Widow should be taking very little damage, so the only Supports that are directly beneficial are those with a way to enhance her such as ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mercy.png)Mercy with damage boost.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: Force her to retreat with dives and flanks. Even if you don’t get the kill, stop her from aiming at your teammates.
Never peek the same angle twice. If you see Widow aiming down sights, don’t walk out at the same position because she will be ready to hit the shot.
Avoid her sightlines. Scout or get info from your team about her position. Then take side routes where she can’t snipe you.

Guide.title: Overview
content: Is your backline being harassed all game by pesky flankers? ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/torbjorn.png)Torbjörn is the answer to all your problems. Equipped with an auto-firing Turret, a long-range projectile, and a shotgun, Torb handles business at all ranges. He contests space almost as good as a Tank, and excels at defending choke points.

Against dive comps, he’ll set up in the back to protect his team, and with brawl comps, he’ll use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/overload.png)Overload shotgun to wipe out the enemy. Even if you struggle to aim his primary, Turret puts in so much work it won’t even matter. In close games that go into Overtime, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/molten-core.png)Molten Core burns up the objective area to get you the win.

Guide.title: Playing As
content: * Protect your backline with Turret by setting it up in corners behind your team.
* Instead of activating Overload just for extra damage, treat it as a counterattack. Surviving the enemy's attack is more important than desperately trying to get one elim.
* Save Molten Core for when the fight is centered on the objective. Force them off the point or burn them up.

Guide.title: Playing Against
content: * Break his Turret first. Try quickly peeking around corners and hiding between your own shots to minimize the Turret's damage.
* Bait out Overload. Soft engage without committing all your long cooldowns, then back up when he’s using Overload. It only lasts five seconds, and you can attack again as soon as it ends.
* Play ranged heroes. Torb is weaker against heroes with range because they can break his Turret from safety and have more consistent damage than his primary fire.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Area control
* Self-sustain
* Anti-diver
* Aim
* Ultimate
* Weaker on attack

Guide.title: Area control
content: Torb is easily the best DPS hero for controlling space angles and map areas. Turret Auto fires on anybody who enters its LoS, Overload gives him the sustain and damage to contest the enemy, and Molten Core literally turns the floor into lava. When Torb has the chance to set up before the enemy team arrives at a location, he is very challenging to take out.

Guide.title: Self-sustaining
content: With armor higher than average health and the ability to heal himself with overhealth every 10 seconds, Torb doesn't need to rely on his team to keep himself alive. Additionally, his Turret protects him and can be used as a shield if needed. Position near a mega health pack and you’ll be set for life.

Guide.title: Anti-dive
content: Turret and Overload are incredible offensive tools to counter dive heroes. Most other heroes try to deal with dive by escaping, but Torb deals with dive by killing them before they can kill him.

Guide.title: Bullet drop
content: Rivet Gun has the worst bullet drop and projectile speed of any weapon in the DPS roster. At medium to long ranges, this makes aiming difficult and hitting shots inconsistent.

Guide.title: Situational ult
content: Torb’s ult won’t always get you insane value. Anytime the enemy has fliers or high mobility heroes, Molten Core’s potential goes way down, as they can easily avoid the affected areas. It’s also not an ult you can just click and get kills with, like many other DPS ults are.

Guide.title: Weaker on attack
content: While he’s one of the best defenders, Torb can struggle to get set up when he’s attacking. If the enemy team already controls the objective or its his team’s turn to push the payload, he doesn’t have time to set up crossfire with his Turret before attacking. Overall, Torb is better at keeping space than he is at taking it.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Rivet Gun
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/rivet-gun.png)Rivet Gun
* Aim high
* * The farther away your target, the higher you’ll have to aim to hit your shots. Even at mid-range, you’ll need to account for bullet drop.
* Aim for or just above their heads to go for the critical hits, or let the bullet drop to hit the body.
* “Head glitch”
* * Technically, you can’t head-glitch in OW, but with Torb, you can shoot and spam crouch on staircases or when on high ground shoot to lower ground enemies.
* Example: Use the trajectory arc to shoot over the staircase when the enemies are on top. Torb can hide behind the stair ground, and his projectiles will drop enough to still hit the enemy.
* Better for armor
* * Against Tanks with lots of armor, primary fire will deal higher damage per second than secondary fire.

Guide.title: Secondary Fire: Rivet Gun (Shotgun)
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/rivet-gun.png)Rivet Gun **(Shotgun)**
* Only for extremely close range
* * Unless you are very close, don’t use the shotgun. The bullet spread will cause too many pellets to miss.
* High burst damage
* * Shotgun can also critical hit. When you manage to barrel stuff and land every pellet, a headshot will one-shot all 250 HP heroes.
* Anti-dive
* * When you’re getting dove, shotgun is easier to land shots with, and the damage will drive the attacker back.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Deploy Turret
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deploy-turret.png)Deploy Turret
* Create crossfire

* * By default, you should place your Turret at a different location than yourself. That way, the enemy has to decide between looking in two different directions if they want to shoot you or the Turret.
* Protect your backline
* * Anytime the enemy team has heroes flanking your backline, you should be placing your Turret in the back where it can protect them.
* As soon as an enemy comes into Turret’s LoS, it will target them. The damage helps win the fight, and the Turret firing also alerts you and your allies that an enemy is nearby.
* Protect your flank

* * Placing your Turret behind yourself can serve two purposes. First off, it can still shoot the enemies in front of you. Secondly, when enemies try to get behind you, the Turret will see them first and start shooting.
* Position it in difficult-to-shoot places
* * Your goal is to make them have to make a choice in looking multiple directions and split their focus.
* They shouldn’t be able to easily corner peek without taking damage.
* High ground, behind weird cover, and so on are usually all good options
* Locks onto primary fire’s target
* * When there are multiple enemies in the Turret’s LoS, it will prioritize the enemy that your primary fire shot hits.

Guide.title: [E]: Overload
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/overload.png)Overload
* Counter enemy aggression
* * The first situation you should be looking to save Overload for is when the enemy starts using their cooldowns to get in close and kill your team.
* Pop Overload to survive their attack and drive them back with your barrage of fast shots.
* Capitalize on offensive openings
* * When your team creates an opening through elims, ult use, or forcing enemy cooldowns, use the movement and attack speed to get run in and finish them off.
* Disengage to live
* * Reengage when you have Turret and Overload back online.

Guide.title: Alternate Weapon: Forge Hammer
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/forge-hammer.png)Forge Hammer
* Heal Turret
* * The main use of Forge Hammer is healing your Turret after it takes damage, but isn’t destroyed.
* Against light amounts of poke, you can heal through the damage and use the Turret like a tiny shield to protect yourself.
* If keeping your Turret up is the priority, then stand in front with your back to the enemy and heal your Turret. Use Overdrive or an ally’s healing to tank the damage.
* Final blows
* * Occasionally, you’ll be dueling an enemy at close range and run out of ammo. In these rare instances, bust out the Hammer and bonk them to death!

Guide.title: Ultimate: Molten Core
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/molten-core.png)Molten Core
* Tap fire to spread out

* * Don't hold down primary fire throughout your entire ult, or else you will waste its very limited ammo. Instead, tap primary fire as you aim at different locations to spread the lava out and cover more of the map.
* Objective contesting
* * Molten Core is particularly good when used on the objective or during overtime when both teams have to touch.
* Cover any objective area the enemy wants to stand on, including the payload.
* Cut off escape
* * As soon as the enemy hears your Molten Core voiceline, they'll likely try to create space and back away.
* Shoot Molten Core behind them to trap them in place or force them to take damage while walking through.

Guide.title: Hammer Time
content: * Best Minor Perk
* Less reload time
* * Focus on not letting your Overdrive get forced out. That way, you can decide when is best to activate and get the instant reload.

Guide.title: Pre-Heated
content: * Best Minor Perk
* Less reload time
* * Focus on not letting your Overdrive get forced out. That way, you can decide when is best to activate and get the instant reload.

Guide.title: Anchor Bolts
content: * Best Major Perk
* High and inconvenient
* * Find places that are way out of the enemy's LoS where they have to look away from your team in order to shoot the Turret.
* Above and behind

* * No enemy is going to be looking above and behind them as they walk through a choke point. Sticking your Turret to the choke point wall won’t shoot the enemy until they come through the choke. But that also means they can’t destroy before walking in.
* New locations
* * When running Anchor Bolts, never just stick your Turret to the floor. Keep changing the location and keep the enemy guessing.

Guide.title: Overloaded Turret
content: * Decent Major Perk
* Overload damage
* * When Torb activates Overload, and this Major Perk causes the Turret to transform into the Overloaded Turret, there is a notable startup animation before the Turret starts firing again.

* Consequently, you don’t even get the extra damage throughout your whole Overload. So, while this Perk can be helpful because of some extra burst damage, it’s very brief and infrequent due to Overload’s cooldown.
* Instant Turret heal
* * The best part of this perk is really the extra Turret health to keep it alive when it's being attacked. You can Overload, run to Turret with Craftsman, and it becomes very tanky.

Guide.title: Maps
content: Torbjörn and his Turrets do best on maps that favor close-range engagements and have choke points that are difficult to break through. When he can set up his Turret behind his team in a position where the enemy team has to walk through a choke to see, it is much harder for them to deal with the Turret. The bullet drop and slow speed of his primary fire put him at a major disadvantage against other ranged heroes on maps with long sight lines.

Although he has decent movement speed from Overload, Torb doesn’t have any vertical mobility. He can deal with the dive comps that traditionally do well on high ground maps, but it's easy for him to fall behind in rotations.

Supports like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/zenyatta.png)Zenyatta and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki who bring high value to your team, but also struggle against flankers are good choices.

For the same reason, sniper DPS also pair well and have the added benefit of making up for Torb's ranged weakness (e.g., ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/widowmaker.png)Widowmaker, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ashe.png)Ashe. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sojourn.png)Sojourn)

For Tanks, he can play fine with dive since he doesn't need a frontline Tank to protect or peel for him (e.g.,![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/winston.png)Winston, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/wrecking-ball.png)Wrecking Ball) . However, in brawl and rush (e.g., ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/junker-queen.png)Junker Queen, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/zarya.png)Zarya) he can use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/overload.png)Overload to go aggro with them and his shotguns melts at close range.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: If you have ranged damage, consider it your job to destroy ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/deploy-turret.png)Deploy Turret every time he sets one up. If left alone, your team will lose. You can quickly peek around corners, shoot, then hide between shots to attack without giving the turret time to lock-on to you.

Bait out ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/overload.png)Overload. Soft engage without committing all your long cooldowns, then back up when he’s using Overload. It only lasts five seconds, and you can attack again as soon as it ends. Consider him unkillable if you haven't seen him already pop the over armor.

To counter-pick, play ranged heroes since ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/torbjorn.png)Torbjörn is weaker against heroes who can position farther away because they can break his Turret from safety and have more consistent damage than his primary fire.
