**DPS:** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sojourn.png)Sojourn, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/echo.png)Echo

**Support:** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/lucio.png)Lúcio

Guide.title: Overview
content: The OG flying hero of Overwatch, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/pharah.png)Pharah, dominates the skies as she rains rockets down on her targets. More movement abilities than any other hero allow her to navigate map terrain in a completely unique way.

If you are just coming back to the game after a few seasons, you may have missed her rework. The rework has made her far more independent and has reduced Pharah's demand on the team's resources, whereas she previously required the near 100% focus of a Support hero like Mercy. The new Pharah has incredibly fast mobility, which allows her to dive enemy backlines, and use environmental cover to counter hitscans and snipers.

Against enemy comps with primarily short-range abilities, Pharah becomes one of the best poke heroes due to ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/rocket-launcher.png)Rocket Launcher having zero falloff damage and good AoE splash damage.

Guide.title: Playing As
content: * Use natural cover from vertical map geometry such as walls and buildings to avoid exposing yourself to hitscan pressure.
* Play around off-angles and on highground so you can spam choke points with crossfire from your team.

* Use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/barrage.png)Barrage from unexpected positions or when coordinated with protection from an ally, such as a ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/projected-barrier.png)Projected Barrier or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/defense-matrix.png)Defense Matrix.

Guide.title: Playing Against
content: * The best way to deal with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/pharah.png)Pharah is to play a hitscan with range and burst damage like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ashe.png)Ashe or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/illari.png)Illari.
* Deny her safe air space by controlling high ground and forcing her to play predictable sightlines.
* Track her Barrage and hold defensive cooldowns or burst abilities to punish her immediately when she commits. A slight delay will make the difference between dying and taking her out.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Vertical mobility
* Excellent at using cover
* Engage + Disengage
* Slow projectiles
* Ult causes own death
* Hitscans

Guide.title: Vertical mobility
content: The ability to take to the sky, fly over buildings, and remain in the air puts Pharah in a league of her own in controlling the vertical plane. For enemies shooting at Pharah, adjusting their aim vertically is generally accepted as being more difficult than horizontal adjustments. Correct usage of ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/hover-jets.png)Hover Jets and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/jump-jet.png)Jump Jet creates consistent pressure from angles that only Pharah can position herself in.

Just the dividing of attention from the enemy team can be enough to make a team with a good Pharah playing feel unstoppable. Her vertical movement also allows her to create pathing options over environments that would typically not be possible for most of the cast.

Guide.title: Excellent at using cover
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/rocket-launcher.png)Rocket Launcher’s slow rate of fire makes Pharah excel at quickly peeking in and out of cover, only exposing herself while firing a rocket. When grounded, she can do this by strafing around a wall. In the air, Hover Jets allow Pharah to use the tops of buildings and structures to peek above, shoot, and dip below to safety.

Guide.title: Quickly engage and disengage
content: Combining Rocket jumps, Jet Dash, and Concussive Blast self-knockback give Pharah access to multiple instances of high bursts of speed. Depending on the map and situation, she can quickly engage or dive a target with one of her cooldowns, get an elimination, then use her remaining abilities to retreat to safety until all her resources are restored.
Cycling Pharah’s movement cooldowns is extremely important for maximizing her impact and potential.

Guide.title: Slow projectile speed
content: From medium to long range, Pharah can struggle to land direct impacts due to the slow projectile speed of ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/rocket-launcher.png)Rocket Launcher. At very long ranges, enemies with movement abilities have plenty of time to reactively dodge incoming rockets.

Pharah players need to become really good at predicting movement in order to maximize damage output. Damage mitigation abilities like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/defense-matrix.png)Defense Matrix and barriers can also be used reactively to prevent any rocket damage from being dealt.

Guide.title: Often dies during her own Ultimate
content: “Justice Rains fro… uggghhhh!” Pharah makes herself into a stationary bullseye while she ults. Headshots, CC abilities, damage mitigation abilities and every attack can easily save enemies from death and eliminate Pharah before she has a chance to move again.

Typically, players will need to coordinate with a teammate if they hope to survive using ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/barrage.png)Barrage. Abilities like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/protection-suzu.png)Protection Suzu and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/projected-barrier.png)Projected Barrier can change Barrage from being deadly to herself to being deadly to the enemy team.

Guide.title: Hitscans
content: While the rework has given ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/pharah.png)Pharah much more counterplay against hitscans, she still can be quickly eliminated by players with good aim mechanics on a hitscan hero.

Pharah has the benefit of mobility and no falloff damage, but these struggle to make up for how reliably and quickly hitscan abilities deal damage to her. Pharah’s normal hover jet movement is rather slow and makes her an easy target for heroes like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ashe.png)Ashe, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/baptiste.png)Baptiste, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mauga.png)Mauga.

Guide.title: Positioning and Playstyle
content: While playstyle ultimately depends on the individual player, the optimal way to play ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/pharah.png)Pharah should always adapt to the map and the enemy team composition.
On maps with strong vertical cover, such as Eichenwalde, you should spend most of your time in the air, abusing rooftops and structures to minimize exposure.
Against brawl, rush, and other close-range comps, maintain distance and continuously pressure grouped enemies, taking full advantage of Rocket Launcher’s AoE splash damage.

When playing into poke comps with multiple hitscan heroes, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/jet-dash.png)Jet Dash toward wider flank angles and spend more time closer to the ground. Open skies become too exposed, so using natural cover and off-angles is critical for survival.

Guide.title: Rocket Launcher
content: Tips for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/rocket-launcher.png)Rocket Launcher
Landing rockets consistently requires prediction.
* Anticipate where enemies want to move.
* Low-health targets will often retreat toward cover—fire at the cover entrance to force them into your rocket.
* Look for predictable movement patterns such as jumps, linear mobility abilities, or falling.
When an enemy is locked into a movement **arc**, fire where they will land. Once airborne or committed to an ability, they cannot alter their trajectory.

Guide.title: Rocket Jump
content: A Rocket Jump uses ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/rocket-launcher.png)Rocket Launcher to give Pharah a small burst of movement in her current direction.

* Can be combined with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/hover-jets.png)Hover Jets, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/jump-jet.png)Jump Jet, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/jet-dash.png)Jet Dash, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/concussive-blast.png)Concussive Blast.
* Provides additional vertical mobility to access positions that would otherwise be unreachable.
* See **Advanced Tech** below for combination examples.

Guide.title: Concussive Blast
content: Tips for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/concussive-blast.png)Concussive Blastthe

Guide.title: Concussive Jump
content: Use the self-knockback from Concussive Blast to launch yourself in a chosen direction.
* The most common use of the ability.
* Primarily horizontal movement, but can also redirect vertically.
* Excellent for repositioning quickly.

Guide.title: Environmental Boops
content: Near map edges, Concussive Blast is a powerful tool for securing eliminations and generating ultimate charge by knocking enemies off the map.

Guide.title: Forcing Vulnerable Positions
content: Use knockback to:
* Separate the enemies from each other
* Knock targets off high ground
* Push enemies into the open away from cover

Guide.title: Preventing Retreat
content: One of the most valuable uses of Concussive Blast is stopping a target from escaping.
If an enemy attempts to disengage by walking away or using a movement ability, use the knockback to keep them exposed. This is extremely effective mid-fight when cleaning up surviving enemies.

Guide.title: Hover Jets
content: Tips for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/hover-jets.png)Hover Jets

Guide.title: Roof Hovering
content: Use rooftops, walls, and map geometry to stall in the air without consuming fuel.
* Excellent for setting up flanks, rollouts, and dive angles.
* Roof peaks can often be balanced on and slid across.
* After using cooldowns to reach rooftops, you can “roof hover” while waiting for CDs to refresh.
* Roof hovering does **not** regenerate fuel.

Guide.title: Jet Dash
content: Tips for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/jet-dash.png)Jet Dash
* Pharah can chain her movement abilities in nearly any sequence. The key is deciding which abilities to use, in what order, and which to hold for disengage.

Guide.title: [Ultimate]: Barrage
content: Tips for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/barrage.png)Barrage

* ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/pharah.png)Pharah needs to be pretty close to quickly kill with her ult. Don't use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/barrage.png)Barrage while flying at max height.

* Using ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/barrage.png)Barrage makes you extremely vulnerable. When possible, ask for ally protection like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/defense-matrix.png)Defense Matrix, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/projected-barrier.png)Projected Barrier or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/protection-suzu.png)Protection Suzu.
* Ideally, you will sneak up on your targets by dropping from high ground or by sliding down a roof or ledge. All her jets are very loud and will alert the enemy to your position.

Guide.title: Dash → Concussive Jump
content: Use ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/jet-dash.png)Jet Dash, then immediately ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/concussive-blast.png)Concussive Blast jump while within blast radius.
* Can stack both abilities in the same direction for long-distance travel.
* Can redirect mid-combo to launch around corners unexpectedly.

Guide.title: Rocket Jump + Dash + Concussive Jump
content: The fastest possible burst of movement.
* Requires near-simultaneous activation.
* Grants both horizontal and vertical distance.
* Often used to dive isolated sniper targets.
* Commonly used to create surprise-angle Barrage setups.

Guide.title: Stair Dash
content: Dash across a slanted surface such as stairs.
* Instead of lifting into the air, Pharah slides along the incline.
* Allows rapid ground-level repositioning.
* Can instantly corner by adjusting camera angle and directional input

Guide.title: Drift Thrusters
content: * Pretty much the only way you can expect to survive using your own ult. While the movement may not look like much, this perk has proven very effective at making Barrage more successful.

Guide.title: Helix Shields
content: * Good self-sustain. Best when you are not able to get consistent healing from your Supports.

Guide.title: Fuel Stores
content: * Allows Pharah to stay in the sky for longer. Best on maps with lots of vertical cover like Watchpoint Gibraltar.

Guide.title: Rocket Salvo
content: * Considering Pharah has two movement abilities, you get to activate the mini-rockets pretty often. Good for extra damage and better AoE.
* New total on direct hit is 200

Guide.title: Eichenwalde
content: The first two points of Eichenwalde give Pharah some of the best opportunities of any map to make massive solo plays. The various rooftops and tall walls can easily be used on both defense and offense to set up flanks and completely disrupt the enemy gameplan. Controlling the high ground on 2nd point is a crucial win condition. Pharah is one the few characters that quickly engage and retreat from the high ground in this area.

Guide.title: Lijiang Tower
content: Control Tower is the worst of the three map areas for Pharah but even it can be quite strong for her. Garden and Night Market are Pharah playgrounds. She can safely spam through windows and over walls where she is extremely difficult for enemies to deal with. With a Mercy pocket on either of these two points, you’d have no excuse if your team loses because Pharah is so dominant and perfectly suited to the environmental archetype of Lijiang Tower.

Guide.title: Shambhali Monastery
content: Shambhali Monastery is another great map for Pharah because its open spaces are all surrounded by the perfect structural cover for a flying hero. When attacking first point, flanking over the building on the left or on the right are both excellent choices for Pharah to fly over and force enemy attention off of her team to allow them to push the cart. The 2nd point also offers multiple flight paths for Pharah to choose from, making it difficult for the enemy team to predict and prepare for her attack.

Guide.title: Samoa
content: None of the three map areas on Samoa provides Pharah with the vertical structures she would like to play around. The control points are also too tight, and are difficult for a flier to set up around without exposing themselves too much. You’ll likely find yourself endlessly poking into a brawl comp without ever getting an elim on this map.

Guide.title: Ilios
content: Although Well is a strong map for Pharah, Ruins and Lighthouse require her to completely outplay her counters in order to be effective. Ruins is overrun by snipers who have a huge advantage over Pharah here. She also struggles to provide point pressure on Lighthouse because of the edge of the map placement, and extreme amount of natural cover provided to heroes positioned directly in the objective area.

Guide.title: Havana
content: Havana has huge open skies, with either little to no cover in the main center areas. Snipers rule the skies on first and third point where Pharah struggles to find any angles to poke and approach from. While she can hug the walls, and play on the outskirts, the map geometry doesn’t play into any of Pharah’s strengths.

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: Pharah’s newfound independence and adaptability allow her to be an effective member of any type of team composition. The ability to stay with her team and poke, or keep up any team's speed and movement mean Pharah is more map dependent than team comp dependent. Dive comps suit her best, however, and enable Pharah to get optimal use of every aspect of her kit. She can support team dives from long range with her rockets, or with a deep off angle flank. In either scenario, Pharah can be used to deal damage that the rest of her team follows up on and confirms elims, or as the one who is following up and getting the final blows.

Guide.title: **Ideal team comp built around :**
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/d-va.png)D.Va, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/pharah.png)Pharah, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/tracer.png)Tracer, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mercy.png)Mercy, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana

Guide.title: Individual synergies with other heroes
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/d-va.png)D.Va

* D.Va pairs well with Pharah primarily because of their flying mobility. Regardless of where an enemy target is positioned, D.Va and Pharah can always find a way to close the gap and reach their mark. While other heroes struggle to keep up with both of these heroes' movements, pairing them together makes that mobility even more deadly. Moreover, D.Va’s Defense Matrix is one of, if not the absolute best way, to guarantee Pharah survives using Barrage. Defense Matrix can give Pharah time to reposition, go aggressive, or peel for her when being focused. The synergy between these two requires some coordination so it may be difficult to pull off effectively without team chat.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sojourn.png)Sojourn

* Although Sojourn can’t fly and isn't a dive hero, her mid-range and long range pressure combined with her Power Slide mobility make Sojourn an excellent choice for the 2nd DPS slot. Rail Gun charges up quickly and outputs constant small pressure. Sojourn can use her mobility to set up angles where she can catch enemies looking up towards Pharah and line up some easy Alt-fire Rail Gun headshots. On just about every map, these two heroes can effectively divide the enemy team’s attention by attacking from opposing angles and both heroes can follow up on the other's aggression when cooldowns are available.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mercy.png)Mercy

* PharMercy. One of the most iconic duos in the entire lifespan of Overwatch. The new version of Pharmercy is quite different than the old. Previously, the duo would permanently fly, poke from long range and off angles, and go off on their own solo mission while the rest of the team worked separately. Currently, Pharah doesn’t need Mercy to work but she still gets massive benefits from having a pocket damage boost and healer that can follow her around. Mercy can often start fights with Pharah positioned low or grounded, and jiggle peeking corners to poke down enemy defenses. Once the opportunity arrives, Damage boosting Pharah’s aggression practically guarantees confirming quick elims before the enemy can react.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: When you find yourself playing into a good Pharah player you primarily need to keep track of two things: where she can engage from, and what LoS she’s trying to use. If you can predict where Pharah might try to use her mobility to engage from, (over a particular wall, or around a certain corner, etc.) then you can catch her off guard and will have a good chance of eliminating her before her CDs refresh and she can escape. If you can keep a lock on the LoS she’s trying to use, you can catch her peeking and hit her while exposed, or position yourself where she is unable to attack you.

Guide.title: Specific Hero Counters
content: ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mauga.png)Mauga

* When playing Tank, Mauga is your best choice for dealing with Pharah. Not only does his hitscan primary fire track on a flying Pharah really well, but once ignited, the extra 2 seconds of damage over time further delays her universal self heal passive from kicking in, thus keeping Pharah out of the fight for longer.
**All Hitscan DPS**

* Which of the Hitscan DPS will be the best counter against Pharah depends on Map and player preference. Long sightline maps like Circuit Royal make Ashe and Widow the best choices. Closer range maps like Arctic Peninsula are better suited to Cassidy or Soldier: 76. The main thing is to understand your heroes' damage fall off ranges and where to position to maximize damage output on the enemy Pharah.
![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/baptiste.png)Baptiste

* Baptiste can burn down Pharah with a few quick bursts of his primary fire. His Exo Boots keep him off the ground and in the air where Pharah has a difficult time landing rockets. Immortality Field is also a strong tool for keeping himself and his teammates alive against Pharah’s rockets and can give extra survivability time to a Barrage for the team to react and shut down the ult.

ashe

Guide.title: Overview
content: The sneaky backline assassin known as ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sombra.png)Sombra is a menace to the unprepared. As soon as hero bans were introduced, she immediately took the #1 spot as the most banned hero, and continues to be a frequent ban. Her ability to become Invisible and prevent her enemies from using their own cooldowns makes her frustrating to play against.

Sombra excels at disrupting the enemy team and forcing out resources to deal with her. Her viability has a bit of a reverse bell curve as lower rank players struggle to deal with her, but her full potential is only seen in coordinated pro play.

Most players have her in their hero pool as a counterpick rather than a starter choice. This is because her kit serves a niche function of interrupting abilities with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/hack.png)Hack, but against heroes who rely on those abilities to play the game, Sombra shuts them down and often forces them to swap to another hero.

Guide.title: Playing As
content: * Translocate first to get into position, stay invisible for the max duration, attack, then immediately Translocate out to stay alive.
* Hack is equally good for initiating a solo attack or for interrupting an enemy attacking your team. Don’t forget to use Hack defensively to help out your allies.

* ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/emp.png)EMP is best used as a combo with another ally’s ult. Check the scoreboard to confirm another offensive ult is available, then wait until that hero is in position to follow up before you EMP.

Guide.title: Playing Against
content: * Be on the lookout for Sombra if you haven’t seen her for a while; that means she’s in position to flank you. Be ready to turn around and counterattack.
* If she Translocates right into your team, assume EMP is coming. CC her, dash away, or get to cover.

* Heroes with mobility like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/d-va.png)D.Va and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/anran.png)Anran can chase after Translocate and shoot Sombra out of invis for the kill.

Guide.title: Strengths And Weaknesses Summarized
content: * Invisible annoyance
* Ability lockout
* Backline assassin
* Low damage
* Stealth duration
* Range

Guide.title: Invisible annoyance
content: Whether or not Sombra is getting elims, she’s always being disruptive to the enemy. The threat of her existence in a backline requires consent, attention and holding onto resources. Against Tanks, getting Hacked is very disruptive so Tanks hate having to play around Sombra.

Guide.title: Ability lockout
content: Both Hack and EMP briefly prevent affected heroes from using any abilities and stop them if they are channelling an ability. As abilities are the most important aspect of any hero's kit, it goes without saying that being able to do this is very strong. Some heroes are completely shut down by a single Hack.

Guide.title: Backline assassin
content: Sombra’s entire kit is perfectly built for assassinating backlines. Supports or Sniper DPS are easy to sneak up on and will generally not be moving too much, and looking straight ahead. The classic, Hack, Virus, shoot combo from behind makes quick work of these isolated enemies.

Guide.title: Low damage
content: Although Sombra can burst down a single target, her overall damage output might be the lowest of any DPS hero. This is partially because she spends so much time out of the fight while invisible and Translocating around. If she’s not Hacking the right target at the right time, she’s holding down her team because her damage certainly won’t be carrying.

Guide.title: Limited stealth duration
content: Unlike the Sombra of yesteryear, the current iteration can only remain invisible for a few seconds. This means she has to Translocate close to her desired invis target. Since Translocator has an audio cue, enemies can be alerted to her presence and know she only has a few seconds before her location is revealed.

Guide.title: Poor range
content: Sombra is only effective at close-range engagements. Hack’s ranged is only 15 meters, and her gun barely deals any damage at that range anyway. Virus can be shot across the map, but its slow speed gives the enemy plenty of time to dodge or block.

Guide.title: Primary Fire: Machine Pistol
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/machine-pistol.png)Machine Pistol
* Best at close range
* * Even though it is a hitscan, the wide spread and damage falloff makes Machine Pistol very weak at medium to long ranges.
* Opportunist damage
* * Because you deal more damage to Hacked enemies, you should try to Hack before firing.
* One-clip
* * When she sneaks up to only a few meters away from her target, Sombra can one clip all DPS and Supports without needing to Virus them.
* You have to land most of the bullets, so the closer the better.
* If the enemy is still alive by the time you run out of bullets, it's generally going to be smarter to Translocate away and not stand there reloading.
* Ranged poke

* * Don’t spend too much time poking the enemy from a distance, you aren’t Soldier: 76. But, when you do, it’s better to fire in short bursts because your bullet spread is all over the place after 6 rapid shots.

Guide.title: Secondary Fire: Hack
content: Tips for ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/hack.png)Hack
* Begin with Hack
* * You’ll want to begin almost every engagement with Hack. Whether you're coming out of invisibility or not, you want to ability lock and trigger Opportunist before using your gun or Virus.
* Hack cancels channelled abilities
* * Examples include Orisa charging up Terra Surge, Junker Queen when she begins Rampage, and Simga as he flies around for Gravitic Flux.
* All these abilities can be cancelled with Hack. When you suspect the enemy has their ult ready to use, try to stay within the distance to react with Hack.
* Hack mega health packs

* * Every control objective has a nearby mega health pack, and all payload paths have a few along the way. Take the extra few seconds to Hack the mega closest to the enemy to prevent them from using it.

Guide.title: [SHIFT]: Virus
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/virus.png)Virus
* Hack before Virus
* * Virus deals extra impact damage, then faster damage over time to enemies currently Hacked. Therefore, you’ll ideally only use Virus after Hacking the enemy.
* Use without Hack
* * Sometimes you don’t have time to get out an uninterrupted Hack. You should still use Virus anyway. It’s very fast and still deals over 100 total damage.
* Destroy deployables
* * Torb’s turret, for example, is a nuisance to your sneaky flank play style. Shoot Virus at it before Translocating in to help your team destroy it faster.

Guide.title: [E]: Translocator
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/translocator.png)Translocator
* Translocate often
* * The short 6-second cooldown starts as soon as you teleport and is ready again just after coming out of invisibility. So use it liberally.
* Dive
* * Translocate above, to the side or behind your target to get into close range and begin attacking immediately.
* Escape
* * Never commit to a fight while Translocate is on cooldown. You need it to survive. Anytime the enemy gets you to low health, focuses you, or attempts to CC you, immediately Translocate away.
* Double Translocate
* * Use Translocator and stealth’s movement buff to get to the closet hiding spot near your target. Then use another Translocator in place just to activate stealth and run up to your desired target.

Guide.title: (Passive): Opportunist
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/opportunist.png)Opportunist
* Communicate enemy ults
* * Enemies who are currently at full ult charge will have a check mark floating above them. Let your team know which heroes have ults ready.
* Enemies with ults ready are high-priority targets. Try to take them out first, or pressure them to use ult early.
* Echo Duplicate

* * If an ally ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/echo.png)Echo ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/duplicate.png)Duplicates the enemy ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sombra.png)Sombra, both of your ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/hack.png)Hacks activate ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/opportunist.png)Opportunist.

Guide.title: Ultimate: EMP
content: **Tips for** ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/emp.png)EMP
* Translocate in
* * The easiest way to get a multihit EMP is to Translocate above and between the enemy team.
* This is also the most dangerous method, so you should still try to approach from an off angle.
* Without Translocator
* * Stealth has a short recovery period before Sombra can use another ability. If the enemy has been countering EMP, set up without stealth.
* Set up on an area above the enemy team, then drop down and immediately activate EMP.
* Shutdown enemy ults

* * A countless number of ults can be directly countered by EMP. Deployable ults like Symmetra’s Barrier get destroyed or disabled, channeled ults can be cancelled, and just preventing ability use essentially counters the rest.

Guide.title: Encrypted Upload
content: * Extra sneaky
* * Use the extra stealth to Hack an enemy, then reposition when they try and turn to attack you. Only commit to revealing yourself with your attack once they're disoriented trying to find you.
* Infinite Invisibility

* * Encrypted Upload increases stealth’s duration to 7 seconds and Translocator is on a 6-second cooldown. So technically, Sombra can Hack and Translocate repeatedly without ever becoming unstealthed.
* Good for Hacking health packs because you make up for lost time with the increased uptime.

Guide.title: CTRL ALT ESC
content: * Situational

* * Most of the time, you are engaging with Translocator, so you already have full health, or you’re getting away from the enemy so you’re not in danger of dying. Therefore, you won’t need the self-healing too often.
* Moreover, you can just wait for the universal healing passive to kick in for a similar effect.
* Does decrease down time between engages.

Guide.title: High-Speed Bandwidth
content: * Decent when paired with flankers who frequently use health packs like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/tracer.png)Tracer and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/wrecking-ball.png)Wrecking Ball.
* Come in clutch in the niche situation of dueling near a health pack.
* Often people grab health packs out of combat, so the impact is low.

Guide.title: Viral Replication
content: * More ult charge
* * Although not as free or consistent, you can deal high amounts of AoE damage through Viral Replication, which also results in faster EMPs.
* Especially good against closely grouped team comps like brawl comps.
* More lethal ultimates

* * As you'll often be hitting a group of enemies with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/emp.png)EMP, the follow-up ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/virus.png)Virus is helpful to your team for converting more elims.

Guide.title: Maps
content: The best maps for Sombra have lots of side rooms for her to set up in. Translocator’s versatile movement enables her to access just about any area on any map, so high ground or flat doesn’t matter too much. Sombra struggles on maps with large, open areas that cannot be easily crossed using Translocator and stealth. These areas impede her effectiveness as a flanker. Likewise, if a sightline is too long for her and doesn’t offer enough side paths, she can get sniped during her approach.

Guide.title: Watchpoint
content: Gibraltar

Guide.title: Team Comp Synergies
content: While ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sombra.png)Sombra can be a solo assassin, she's much more effective when paired with at least one other dive hero. Hack-fist is an old term referring to the pairing of ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/doomfist.png)Doomfist and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sombra.png)Sombra; a name they earned because of their lethality and the difficulty of countering their set up.
No matter dive hero, the strategy is the same:

1. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sombra.png)Sombra initiates with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/hack.png)Hack
2. 1. locking the enemy from using abilities

3. The ally (e.g., ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/doomfist.png)Doomfist, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/echo.png)Echo, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/genji.png)Genji) immediately moves in for the kill.
4. ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sombra.png)Sombra and teammates disengage, then repeat on next target.

This strategy works particularly well on heroes who rely on their abilities to counter flanks and dives like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/ana.png)Ana with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/sleep-dart.png)Sleep Dart, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/mizuki.png)Mizuki with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/binding-chain.png)Binding Chain or ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/cassidy.png)Cassidy with ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/flashbang.png)Flashbang.

Guide.title: How to Counter
content: The way ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/sombra.png)Sombra wins games is by harassing backlines and going for sneaky assassinations, then ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/translocator.png)Translocator away to survive. This is the main thing you need to stop if you want to beat her.

Breaking LoS on ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/hack.png)Hack will stop the ability. You can do this by walking behind cover or putting a shield like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/barrier-shield.png)Barrier Shield between you and Sombra. Shooting her also interrupts Hack.
Be on the lookout for Sombra if you haven’t seen her for a while; that means she’s in position to flank you. Be ready to turn around and counterattack.

Equally as important is to watch for her retreat. You can see the line of ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/translocator.png)Translocator and immediately dash or fly to it and attack. When you hit her she'll be revealed for an easy kill. Heroes with mobility like ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/d-va.png)D.Va, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/winston.png)Winston, ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/echo.png)Echo, and ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/heroes/anran.png)Anran are especially good at this.

If she ![](https://cdn.mobalytics.gg/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=96/assets/overwatch/images/abilities/translocator.png)Translocators right into your team, assume EMP is coming. CC her, dash away, or get to cover.
